```text
splunkctl parsers import --path <FILE.yml> [--yes]
splunkctl parsers reload [--conf props|transforms|all] [--yes]
```

### Workflow

#### List source types and extractions

```bash
splunkctl parsers sourcetypes
splunkctl parsers sourcetypes --filter firewall
splunkctl parsers extractions
splunkctl parsers extractions --sourcetype firewall
```

Expected result: one row per `props.conf` stanza with its `category`, or one row per `transforms.conf` stanza. `--filter` is a case-insensitive name substring; `--limit` and `--offset` apply after filtering.

#### Inspect one source type

```bash
splunkctl parsers get syslog
splunkctl parsers get syslog --explicit --app search
splunkctl parsers get my_extraction --conf transforms
splunkctl parsers get mysource --json | jq .
```

Expected result: the merged view of the stanza by default; `--explicit` shows only the keys set in that stanza within `--app` (default `search`). Use `--json` output to diff a source type between dev and prod.

#### Audit every extraction

```bash
splunkctl parsers extractions --json > extractions.json
```

Expected result: a JSON array of every `transforms.conf` stanza with its keys, ready to diff against another instance.

#### Create a source type

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: a new `props.conf` stanza that the indexer uses for events arriving with that source type. Preview with `splunkctl parsers create --sourcetype firewall_appliance_v2 --category Network_Security`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl parsers get firewall_appliance_v2`.

```bash
splunkctl parsers create --sourcetype firewall_appliance_v2 --category Network_Security
splunkctl parsers create --sourcetype firewall_appliance_v2 --category Network_Security --yes
splunkctl parsers create --sourcetype mysource --category Custom --transforms my_extraction --yes
splunkctl parsers get firewall_appliance_v2
```

Expected result: the stanza exists with the category and, when given, a `TRANSFORMS` reference to the extraction.

#### Set or clear parsing keys

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: parsing keys such as `TIME_FORMAT` or `LINE_BREAKER` change how new events are broken and parsed; a wrong `LINE_BREAKER` merges or splits events. Preview with `splunkctl parsers set mysource TIME_FORMAT=%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl parsers get mysource --explicit`.

```bash
splunkctl parsers set mysource TIME_FORMAT=%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S SHOULD_LINEMERGE=false --yes
splunkctl parsers set my_extraction 'REGEX=user=(?<user>\S+)' 'FORMAT=user::$1' --conf transforms --yes
splunkctl parsers set mysource EXTRACT-ip='(?<ip>\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+)' --sharing global --yes
splunkctl parsers unset mysource SHOULD_LINEMERGE --yes
```

Expected result: the keys appear in `get --explicit`. New stanzas are created when missing (`--no-create` turns that off) and are app-shared by default, because user-private parsing stanzas do not apply at index time. The REST API cannot remove a key, so `unset` sets it to the empty string, which disables most parsing keys.

#### Update or delete a source type

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: `update` changes the category or transforms reference; `delete` removes the stanza and events for that source type fall back to default parsing. Preview with `splunkctl parsers delete mysource`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl parsers sourcetypes --filter mysource`.

```bash
splunkctl parsers update mysource --category Operating_System --yes
splunkctl parsers delete mysource
splunkctl parsers delete mysource --yes
```

Export the stanza first (next step) so you can import it again if needed.

#### Export stanzas to YAML

```bash
splunkctl parsers export --path parsers.yml
splunkctl parsers export --path props.yml --conf props --filter firewall
```

Expected result: a YAML file of explicitly set keys only (merged defaults are left out), suitable for version control.

#### Import stanzas from YAML

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: stanzas in the file are created or updated; nothing is deleted. Preview with `splunkctl parsers import --path parsers.yml` and read the per-stanza create, update, or unchanged lines with their key-level diffs, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl parsers get <SOURCETYPE> --explicit`.

```bash
splunkctl parsers import --path parsers.yml
splunkctl parsers import --path parsers.yml --yes
```

Expected result: each stanza reports `create`, `update`, or `unchanged`. The command exits non-zero when any stanza is skipped or fails, so CI cannot silently pass a broken file.

#### Reload props and transforms

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: splunkd re-reads `props.conf` and `transforms.conf`, so index-time changes start applying to new data. Preview with `splunkctl parsers reload`, apply with `splunkctl parsers reload --yes`, and verify by searching a few new events for the expected fields.

```bash
splunkctl parsers reload --yes
splunkctl parsers reload --conf transforms --yes
```

Expected result: index-time keys take effect for data indexed after the reload. Already indexed events are not reparsed.

### Troubleshooting

- `not_found` on `get`, `update`, or `delete`: the name is case-sensitive; copy it from `splunkctl parsers sourcetypes --filter <part>`.
- `permission` on `create`, `set`, or `import`: the account cannot write to the app; use a role with write access, or pass `--sharing app` with an app you own.
- `import` exits 1 while most stanzas applied: at least one stanza was skipped or failed; fix the reported stanza and rerun, the others are idempotent.
- A new `TIME_FORMAT` or `LINE_BREAKER` has no effect: run `splunkctl parsers reload --yes`, then check only events indexed after the reload.
- An `EXTRACT-*` key set by a user-private stanza never fires at index time: promote it with `--sharing app` or `--sharing global`.

### See also

- [Manage configuration as code](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/state.md), which pulls and pushes `parsers.yml`
- [Edit any conf file](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/conf.md)
- [Manage lookups](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/lookups.md)
- [Run searches](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/search.md)
- [Command reference: parsers](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/parsers.md)

## Set up and check SOAR

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md


When to use: you are connecting splunkctl to a Splunk SOAR instance for the first time, or you need a quick read of its health, license usage, settings, or SOC metrics before doing incident work.

### Prerequisites

- A Splunk SOAR instance (on-premises or cloud) reachable on its REST port (default 8443).
- An automation token, or a username and password. Username and password are required for `delete` commands, because SOAR refuses automation tokens on DELETE; custom lists are the exception and accept a token.
- splunkctl installed (see [Install](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/install.md)).

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl config init --soar [--profile NAME]
splunkctl soar test
splunkctl soar info
splunkctl soar health
splunkctl soar license
splunkctl soar settings [--section NAME]
splunkctl soar stats [--widget NAME] [--list]
splunkctl soar meta <severities|statuses|labels|tags|cef|features>
splunkctl soar search <TEXT> [--categories LIST] [--page-size N] [--page N]
```

### Workflow

#### Add SOAR credentials to the profile

```bash
splunkctl config init --soar
splunkctl --profile uat config init --soar
```

The prompts ask for host, port, and either a token or a username and password. Values are saved as a `soar:` map inside the profile, next to the SIEM settings. Environment variables (`SOAR_HOST`, `SOAR_PORT`, `SOAR_TOKEN`, `SOAR_USER`, `SOAR_PASS`) override the profile for one run. Resolution order: environment variables, then the profile `soar:` section, then defaults (port 8443, TLS verification on).

This writes a local file and is not guarded.

#### Verify connectivity

```bash
splunkctl soar test
splunkctl soar test --json
```

Expected result: `status: ok` and the SOAR version. On failure the command prints a typed error envelope (`kind: auth`, `connection`, or `timeout`) and exits 1.

#### Read version and system info

```bash
splunkctl soar info
```

Merges `/rest/version` and `/rest/system_info` into one row: version, FQDN, and system details.

#### Check health

```bash
splunkctl soar health
splunkctl soar health --json
```

Rolls up three endpoints into rows tagged by `type`:

- `daemon` rows from `/rest/health`: the latest state per daemon (decided, nginx, postgres, uwsgi, and others).
- `warm_standby` from `/rest/warm_standby`: `off` on most installs; errors are reported as `unavailable`.
- `cluster_node` from `/rest/cluster_node`: errors are reported as `unclustered` on single-node installs.

#### Check license usage

```bash
splunkctl soar license
```

Shows license type (community or enterprise), the daily action cap (`max_allowed_actions_per_day`), expiry, and today's action count. A community license caps at 100 actions per day, which matters before a bulk `soar actions run`.

#### Read settings and SOC metrics

```bash
splunkctl soar settings
splunkctl soar settings --section debug_settings
splunkctl soar stats
splunkctl soar stats --widget roi_summary
splunkctl soar stats --list
```

`settings` is a read-only dump of `/rest/system_settings`, one row per section (`auth_settings`, `response_settings`, `debug_settings`, `email_settings`, and the rest). `stats` reads `/rest/widget_data/<name>`; without `--widget` it fetches `container_stats`, `containers_workload`, `sla_stats`, and `pending_approvals`. `--list` prints the widget names without calling the API.

#### Look up vocabularies

```bash
splunkctl soar meta severities
splunkctl soar meta statuses
splunkctl soar meta labels
splunkctl soar meta tags
splunkctl soar meta cef
splunkctl soar meta features
```

`statuses` shows the name-to-id map; container updates take the status name, not the id. `labels` cannot be created through the REST API, only in the UI. `features` lists feature flags with their enabled state.

#### Search across objects

```bash
splunkctl soar search dns
splunkctl soar search dns --categories app,container
splunkctl soar search dns --page-size 5 --page 2
```

Free-text search across apps, containers, artifacts, assets, and other object types through `/rest/search`. Each hit carries `category`, `name`, `id`, and `url`. Pagination here is 1-based, unlike other SOAR endpoints.

### Troubleshooting

- `kind: auth` from `soar test`: the token or password is wrong, or the token lacks REST access. Rerun `splunkctl config init --soar`.
- `kind: connection`: check host, port (8443 by default), and TLS. Set `--no-verify` in `config init` only for lab instances with self-signed certificates.
- `kind: auth` on a delete command while reads work: the profile is token-only. Add a username and password.
- `health` shows `unavailable` or `unclustered`: expected on single-node installs without warm standby.

Error kinds match the SIEM taxonomy: `auth`, `connection`, `timeout`, `not_found`, `permission`, `usage`, `error`. See [Exit codes](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/exit-codes.md).

### See also

- [Work SOAR incidents](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-incidents.md)
- [Configure](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/configure.md)
- [Install SOAR apps](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-apps.md)
- [Administer SOAR users and roles](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-admin.md)
- [Command reference: soar](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/soar.md)

## Work SOAR incidents

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-incidents.md


When to use: you are handling an event or case in Splunk SOAR and want to list the queue, pull one container's detail, add evidence (artifacts, files, notes), reassign it, or close it, alone or in bulk.

### Prerequisites

- SOAR credentials in the active profile and a passing `splunkctl soar test` (see [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)).
- Username and password credentials for any `delete` command; SOAR refuses automation tokens on DELETE.
- Status names from `splunkctl soar meta statuses` and label names from `splunkctl soar meta labels`.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl soar containers list [--label TEXT] [--status NAME] [--severity NAME] [--owner USER] [--since DATE] [--type event|case] [--filter DJANGO_FILTER] [--limit N] [--offset N]
splunkctl soar containers get <CONTAINER_ID> [--artifacts|--notes|--comments|--audit|--activity|--playbook-runs|--phases]
splunkctl soar containers create --name <NAME> --label <LABEL> [--severity NAME] [--sensitivity NAME] [--sdi TEXT] [--description TEXT] [--tag TAG]... [--field KEY=VALUE]... [--yes]
splunkctl soar containers update <IDS>... [--status NAME] [--severity NAME] [--owner USER] [--role ROLE] [--tag TAG]... [--field KEY=VALUE]... [--yes]
splunkctl soar containers close <IDS>... [--yes]
splunkctl soar containers assign <IDS>... (--owner USER | --role ROLE) [--yes]
splunkctl soar containers delete <IDS>... [--yes]

splunkctl soar artifacts list --container <CONTAINER_ID> [--limit N] [--offset N]
splunkctl soar artifacts get <ARTIFACT_ID>
splunkctl soar artifacts create --container <CONTAINER_ID> --name <NAME> [--cef KEY=VALUE]... [--cef-file FILE.json] [--cef-type FIELD=TYPE]... [--sdi TEXT] [--severity NAME] [--type TEXT] [--no-automation] [--yes]
splunkctl soar artifacts update <ARTIFACT_ID> [--cef KEY=VALUE]... [--cef-file FILE.json] [--replace-cef] [--name TEXT] [--severity NAME] [--type TEXT] [--yes]
splunkctl soar artifacts delete <ARTIFACT_ID> [--yes]

splunkctl soar vault list [--container CONTAINER_ID]
splunkctl soar vault get <VAULT_ID>
splunkctl soar vault upload --container <CONTAINER_ID> <FILE_PATH> [--yes]
splunkctl soar vault download <VAULT_ID> [--out FILE]
splunkctl soar vault delete <ATTACHMENT_ID> [--yes]

splunkctl soar notes list --container <CONTAINER_ID> [--task TASK_ID]
splunkctl soar notes add --container <CONTAINER_ID> --title <TITLE> [CONTENT] [--file FILE] [--task-id TASK_ID] [--yes]
splunkctl soar notes delete <NOTE_ID> [--yes]
splunkctl soar notes comment <CONTAINER_ID> <TEXT> [--yes]
```

### Workflow

#### Find the containers you need

```bash
splunkctl soar containers list --status open --severity high
splunkctl soar containers list --label events --since 2026-07-01
splunkctl soar containers list --owner admin --type case
splunkctl soar containers list --filter '_filter_name__icontains="dns"'
splunkctl soar containers list --limit 10 --offset 20 --json
```

Filters combine with AND. `--status` is validated against `/rest/container_status` before the query; an unknown name exits 1. `--type event` maps to `container_type=default`. `--since` maps to `_filter_create_time__gt`. `--filter` passes a raw Django-style filter. `--offset` requires `--limit` and must be a multiple of it, because the API pages by page number.

#### Read one container

```bash
splunkctl soar containers get 42
splunkctl soar containers get 42 --artifacts
splunkctl soar containers get 42 --playbook-runs
splunkctl soar containers get 42 --audit --json
```

Without a flag you get the full container object. Each flag fetches one sub-view from `/rest/container/<id>/<suffix>`; if you pass several, the last one wins.

#### Create a container

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: a new container is created with `run_automation: false`, so playbooks do not fire. Preview with `splunkctl soar containers create --name "DNS Alert" --label events`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar containers list --label events --since <today>`.

```bash
splunkctl soar containers create --name "DNS Alert" --label events
splunkctl soar containers create --name "DNS Alert" --label events \
  --severity high --sensitivity white --sdi "SDI-001" \
  --description "Probe" --tag malware --field priority=P1 --yes
```

When `--sdi` is given, the CLI first looks for an existing container with that source data identifier and exits 1 with `kind: conflict` and the existing id if one is found.

#### Update, assign, or close containers

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: status, severity, owner, tags, or fields change on every id you pass, in one bulk request. Preview with `splunkctl soar containers update 42 --severity critical`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar containers get 42`.

```bash
splunkctl soar containers update 42 --severity critical --yes
splunkctl soar containers update 1 2 3 --severity low --yes
splunkctl soar containers update 42 --tag new_tag --yes
splunkctl soar containers assign 42 --owner analyst --yes
splunkctl soar containers assign 1 2 --role analyst --yes
splunkctl soar containers close 42 --yes
```

`--status` takes a name (`closed`), never a numeric id. Tags are read-modify-write: existing tags are fetched at apply time and merged. `assign` takes an owner or a role, not both; names resolve to ids at apply time and every container is read back to confirm the change. `close` is shorthand for `update --status closed`.

#### Delete containers

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the container and all artifacts, vault files, comments, notes, phases, and tasks in it are removed; there is no undo. Preview with `splunkctl soar containers delete 42`, apply with `splunkctl soar containers delete 42 --yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar containers get 42` (expect `not_found`).

```bash
splunkctl soar containers delete 42
splunkctl soar containers delete 42 --yes
```

Requires username and password credentials.

#### Add and update artifacts

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: a new artifact on the container, which can trigger playbooks unless you pass `--no-automation`. Preview with `splunkctl soar artifacts create --container 42 --name "Suspicious IP" --cef sourceAddress=10.0.0.5`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar artifacts list --container 42`.

```bash
splunkctl soar artifacts list --container 42
splunkctl soar artifacts create --container 42 --name "Suspicious IP" \
  --cef sourceAddress=10.0.0.5 --yes
splunkctl soar artifacts create --container 42 --name "DNS hit" \
  --cef destinationDnsDomain=evil.example --severity high --type network \
  --sdi "SDI-001" --no-automation --yes
splunkctl soar artifacts update 77 --cef sourceAddress=9.9.9.9 --yes
splunkctl soar artifacts update 77 --cef sourceAddress=9.9.9.9 --replace-cef --yes
```

CEF fields come from `--cef` (repeatable) and/or `--cef-file`; `--cef` wins on conflict. Contains types are filled in from a built-in CEF map (for example `sourceAddress` becomes `ip` and `host name`); `--cef-type field=type` overrides one entry. SOAR does not deduplicate artifacts by SDI, so when `--sdi` is given the CLI checks for an existing match in the same container and warns. `update` merges CEF keys by default; `--replace-cef` replaces the whole CEF map.

#### Delete an artifact

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the artifact is removed from its container. Preview with `splunkctl soar artifacts delete 77`, apply with `splunkctl soar artifacts delete 77 --yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar artifacts list --container 42`.

```bash
splunkctl soar artifacts delete 77 --yes
```

#### Attach and retrieve vault files

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the file is stored in the vault and attached to the container. Preview with `splunkctl soar vault upload --container 42 ./sample.pcap`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar vault list --container 42`.

```bash
splunkctl soar vault upload --container 42 ./sample.pcap --yes
splunkctl soar vault list --container 42
splunkctl soar vault get <VAULT_ID>
splunkctl soar vault download <VAULT_ID> --out ./sample.pcap
```

Upload base64-encodes the file and posts to `/rest/container_attachment`; files over 30 MB trigger a warning because SOAR's proxy caps requests near 32 MB. `get` and `download` take the vault id (SHA1 hash). `download` without `--out` writes raw bytes to stdout; `--out` overwrites the target without prompting.

#### Delete a vault file

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the attachment is removed from the container. Preview with `splunkctl soar vault delete <ATTACHMENT_ID>`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar vault list --container 42`.

```bash
splunkctl soar vault delete <ATTACHMENT_ID> --yes
```

Use the attachment id (the `id` column of `vault list`), not the vault id hash. Requires username and password credentials.

#### Record notes and comments

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: a note or comment is added to the container. `notes delete` and `notes comment-delete` remove one permanently and need username and password credentials; preview them the same way before adding `--yes`. Preview with `splunkctl soar notes add --container 42 --title "Summary" "Findings"`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar notes list --container 42`.

```bash
splunkctl soar notes list --container 42
splunkctl soar notes list --container 42 --task 7
splunkctl soar notes add --container 42 --title "Summary" "Investigation findings" --yes
splunkctl soar notes add --container 42 --title "Report" --file ./report.md --yes
splunkctl soar notes add --container 42 --title "Task note" --task-id 7 "Task analysis" --yes
splunkctl soar notes delete 10 --yes
splunkctl soar notes comment 42 "Investigation complete" --yes
```

Note content comes from the positional argument or `--file`; `--file` wins when both are given. `--task-id` makes it a task note. `notes comment-delete` exists only to explain that SOAR comments are immutable; it makes no API call.

### Troubleshooting

- `usage` error on `--status`: pass the status name from `splunkctl soar meta statuses`, not a number.
- `kind: conflict` on create: a container with that `--sdi` already exists; the message includes its id.
- `kind: auth` on a delete while reads work: the profile is token-only. Add a username and password with `splunkctl config init --soar`.
- `--offset` rejected: it must be a multiple of `--limit`.
- `assign` exits 1 after a 200 response: the server accepted but ignored the write; the read-back check caught it. Confirm the owner or role exists with `splunkctl soar users list` or `splunkctl soar roles list`.
- Vault delete returns 405: you passed the vault id hash; use the attachment id from `vault list`.

### See also

- [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)
- [Run playbooks](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-playbooks.md)
- [Run actions](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-actions.md)
- [Manage cases and workbooks](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-cases.md)
- [Ingest SIEM results into SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-ingest.md)
- [Command reference: soar](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/soar.md)

## Install SOAR apps

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-apps.md


When to use: you need to see which apps a SOAR instance has, read the configuration keys an app expects before creating an asset, or install or remove an app package.

### Prerequisites

- SOAR credentials in the active profile (`splunkctl config init --soar`) and a passing `splunkctl soar test`.
- `uninstall` requires username and password credentials. SOAR refuses automation tokens on DELETE, so a token-only profile fails with a `kind: auth` error.
- `install` needs a local `.tgz` package from the Splunk SOAR app store or an app developer build.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl soar apps list [--installed] [--category TEXT] [--limit N]
splunkctl soar apps get <APP_ID> [--actions]
splunkctl soar apps install <PATH> [--yes]
splunkctl soar apps uninstall <NAME_OR_ID> [--yes]
```

### Workflow

#### Find the app

```bash
splunkctl soar apps list --installed
splunkctl soar apps list --category SIEM
splunkctl soar apps list --json
```

`--installed` excludes staged apps (uploaded but not configured). `--category` filters by the app's category string. Expected result: one row per app with its id, name, version, and install status.

#### Read the configuration schema

```bash
splunkctl soar apps get 5
splunkctl soar apps get 5 --actions
```

The `configuration` map lists each key with `data_type` (string, password, numeric, boolean), `required`, and `default`. These are the keys you pass to `soar assets create --set` (see [Configure assets and monitor ingestion](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-assets.md)). `--actions` appends the supported actions from `/rest/app/<id>/actions` under an `actions` key.

#### Install an app

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: a new app appears as staged on the instance. Preview with `splunkctl soar apps install myapp.tgz`, apply with `splunkctl soar apps install myapp.tgz --yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar apps list`.

```bash
splunkctl soar apps install myapp.tgz
splunkctl soar apps install myapp.tgz --yes
```

The file is base64-encoded and posted to `/rest/app`. The new app shows as staged until you configure and activate it in the SOAR UI.

#### Uninstall an app

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the app and its assets stop working. Preview with `splunkctl soar apps uninstall DNS`, apply with `splunkctl soar apps uninstall DNS --yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar apps list --installed`.

```bash
splunkctl soar apps uninstall DNS
splunkctl soar apps uninstall 42 --yes
```

A name is resolved to an id through the API before the DELETE.

### Troubleshooting

- `kind: auth` on uninstall: the profile has only an automation token. Add a username and password with `splunkctl config init --soar`.
- The app does not appear in `list --installed` after install: it is staged. Configure and activate it in the SOAR UI, or drop `--installed` to see it.
- `kind: not_found` on uninstall by name: run `splunkctl soar apps list` and use the numeric id.

### See also

- [Configure assets and monitor ingestion](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-assets.md)
- [Run actions](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-actions.md)
- [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)
- [Command reference: soar](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/soar.md)

## Configure assets and monitor ingestion

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-assets.md


When to use: you are wiring a SOAR app to a real service (a DNS resolver, a threat-intel feed, a SIEM poller) and need to create or change its asset, prove it can connect, and confirm ingestion keeps running.

### Prerequisites

- SOAR credentials in the active profile (`splunkctl config init --soar`) and a passing `splunkctl soar test`.
- The app id and its configuration keys, from `splunkctl soar apps get <APP_ID>` (see [Install SOAR apps](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-apps.md)).
- `delete` requires username and password credentials; SOAR refuses automation tokens on DELETE.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl soar assets list [--limit N]
splunkctl soar assets get <ASSET_ID>
splunkctl soar assets create --name <NAME> --app-id <APP_ID> [--set KEY=VALUE]... [--file CONFIG.json] [--description TEXT] [--yes]
splunkctl soar assets update <ASSET_ID> [--set KEY=VALUE]... [--file CONFIG.json] [--name TEXT] [--description TEXT] [--replace] [--yes]
splunkctl soar assets test <ASSET_ID> [--timeout SECONDS] [--yes]
splunkctl soar assets delete <ASSET_ID> [--yes]
splunkctl soar ingest-status
```

### Workflow

#### Inspect existing assets

```bash
splunkctl soar assets list
splunkctl soar assets get 1 --json
```

Expected result: one row per asset with id, name, app, and whether it is configured for ingestion.

#### Create an asset

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: a new asset is created and, if the app polls, may start ingesting containers. Preview with `splunkctl soar assets create --name my_dns --app-id 5 --set dns_server=8.8.8.8`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar assets get <ASSET_ID>`.

```bash
splunkctl soar assets create --name my_dns --app-id 5 \
  --set dns_server=8.8.8.8 --description "Google DNS"
splunkctl soar assets create --name my_dns --app-id 5 \
  --set dns_server=8.8.8.8 --description "Google DNS" --yes
splunkctl soar assets create --name enrichment --app-id 10 --file config.json --yes
```

Configuration comes from `--set key=value` (repeatable) and/or `--file` (a JSON object). When both are given, `--set` wins. Values whose key contains `password`, `secret`, `token`, or `api_key` are shown as `****` in the preview; the real value is sent on `--yes`.

#### Update an asset

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the asset's configuration changes; with `--replace`, every key you do not pass is removed. Preview with `splunkctl soar assets update 1 --set dns_server=1.1.1.1`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar assets get 1`.

```bash
splunkctl soar assets update 1 --set dns_server=1.1.1.1
splunkctl soar assets update 1 --set dns_server=1.1.1.1 --yes
splunkctl soar assets update 1 --name renamed --description "new" --yes
splunkctl soar assets update 1 --replace --set only_key=value --yes
```

The SOAR API treats asset POST as a full replace. By default the CLI fetches the current asset, merges your keys into its configuration, and posts the result, so an update cannot wipe keys by accident. `--replace` skips the merge and sends only what you pass.

#### Test connectivity

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: SOAR runs the app's test-connectivity action against the asset's configured service. Preview with `splunkctl soar assets test 1`, apply with `splunkctl soar assets test 1 --yes`, and verify the result in the command output or on the asset page in the SOAR UI.

```bash
splunkctl soar assets test 1 --yes
splunkctl soar assets test 1 --timeout 60 --yes
```

The command posts to `/rest/asset/<id>/test` and polls `/rest/app_status` for up to `--timeout` seconds (default 30). Expected result: `success` or `failed`. The test runs in the SOAR backend with no visible action run; if polling times out, it may still finish server side, so check the asset page in the SOAR UI.

#### Delete an asset

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the asset is removed and any ingestion or playbook action that used it stops. Preview with `splunkctl soar assets delete 1`, apply with `splunkctl soar assets delete 1 --yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar assets list`.

```bash
splunkctl soar assets delete 1
splunkctl soar assets delete 1 --yes
```

#### Monitor ingestion

```bash
splunkctl soar ingest-status
splunkctl soar ingest-status --json
```

Each row is a poller record from `/rest/ingestion_status` (asset, app, status, message, container label) enriched with `app_status` and `app_message` from `/rest/app_status`. Expected result: every ingestion asset you rely on shows an active status with no error message.

### Troubleshooting

- `kind: auth` on delete: add username and password to the SOAR profile with `splunkctl config init --soar`.
- Test reports a timeout: the command polls at most 12 times, about 30 seconds in total, even with a higher `--timeout`. Check the asset page in the SOAR UI for the final result.
- Keys you set are rejected: compare them with `splunkctl soar apps get <APP_ID>`; names and types must match the app schema.
- A poller shows an error in `ingest-status`: fix the asset configuration with `soar assets update`, rerun `soar assets test`, then check `ingest-status` again.

### See also

- [Install SOAR apps](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-apps.md)
- [Run actions](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-actions.md)
- [Ingest SIEM results into SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-ingest.md)
- [Command reference: soar](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/soar.md)

## Run playbooks

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-playbooks.md


When to use: you want to run a playbook against a container and watch it finish, enable or disable playbooks and set their triggers, or keep playbooks as code: export the bundle, edit the Python in git, and import it back.

### Prerequisites

- SOAR credentials in the active profile and a passing `splunkctl soar test` (see [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)).
- Username and password credentials for `delete`; SOAR 8.5 exposes no working REST deletion, so the CLI logs in through the Web UI, which refuses automation tokens.
- A container id for `run` (`splunkctl soar containers list`).
- For `import`: a playbook bundle, either a `.tgz` or a directory with `<name>.json` (metadata, COA graph, labels, trigger config) and `<name>.py` (Python code with `@phantom.playbook_block()` functions).

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl soar playbooks list [--active] [--label LABEL] [--repo NAME]
splunkctl soar playbooks get <PLAYBOOK_ID>
splunkctl soar playbooks enable <PLAYBOOK_ID> [--yes]
splunkctl soar playbooks disable <PLAYBOOK_ID> [--cancel-runs] [--yes]
splunkctl soar playbooks trigger <PLAYBOOK_ID> --on <artifact_created|container_resolved> [--yes]
splunkctl soar playbooks run <PLAYBOOK_ID_OR_NAME> --container <CONTAINER_ID> [--scope all|new] [--input KEY=VALUE]... [--wait] [--timeout SECONDS] [--yes]
splunkctl soar playbooks runs list [--container CONTAINER_ID] [--status pending|running|success|failed] [--limit N]
splunkctl soar playbooks runs get <RUN_ID> [--blocks]
splunkctl soar playbooks runs cancel <RUN_ID> [--yes]
splunkctl soar playbooks export <PLAYBOOK_ID_OR_NAME> [--out DIR] [--unpack]
splunkctl soar playbooks import <PATH.tgz | DIR/> [--scm NAME] [--force|--no-force] [--yes]
splunkctl soar playbooks delete <PLAYBOOK_ID_OR_NAME>... [--yes]
splunkctl soar playbooks repos
splunkctl soar playbooks sync <REPO_ID> [--yes]
```

### Workflow

#### List and inspect playbooks

```bash
splunkctl soar playbooks list
splunkctl soar playbooks list --active
splunkctl soar playbooks list --label events
splunkctl soar playbooks list --repo local
splunkctl soar playbooks get 10 --json
```

Expected result: filters combine with AND. `--active` uses the SOAR boolean filter (`_filter_active=True`), `--label` matches the playbook's `labels[]` array, `--repo` filters by SCM repo name. `get` returns the full object including the `coa` graph, labels, trigger configuration, and `draft_mode`.

#### Run a playbook against a container

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the playbook's blocks execute against the container's artifacts, including any containment actions it contains. Preview with `splunkctl soar playbooks run my_playbook --container 42` and read the POST body, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar playbooks runs list --container 42`.

```bash
splunkctl soar playbooks run my_playbook --container 42 --yes
splunkctl soar playbooks run 7 --container 42 --yes
splunkctl soar playbooks run my_playbook --container 42 \
  --scope new --input ip=1.2.3.4 --input domain=evil.com --yes
splunkctl soar playbooks run my_playbook --container 42 \
  --wait --timeout 120 --yes
```

Expected result: a `POST /rest/playbook_run` with `{playbook_id, container_id, scope, run: true, inputs?}` and the run id. A name is resolved through `GET /rest/playbook?_filter_name=...`. `--scope all` (default) runs against every artifact in the container; `new` limits to artifacts not yet processed. `--wait` polls `GET /rest/playbook_run/<id>` until the status reaches `success`, `failed`, or `cancelled` (default timeout 300 seconds); when the `message` field parses as JSON it is pretty-printed. A bogus playbook id returns 404 `"Playbook \"N\" not found"`; the server validates the id before creating a run.

#### Monitor and cancel runs

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: `runs cancel` stops an in-progress run part way through its blocks. Preview with `splunkctl soar playbooks runs cancel 101`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar playbooks runs get 101`.

```bash
splunkctl soar playbooks runs list
splunkctl soar playbooks runs list --container 42 --status failed
splunkctl soar playbooks runs get 101
splunkctl soar playbooks runs get 101 --blocks
splunkctl soar playbooks runs cancel 101 --yes
```

Expected result: `runs get` shows the run detail; `--blocks` adds per-block status and output from `/rest/playbook_run/<id>/block_results`; `cancel` posts `{cancel: true}` to the run.

#### Enable, disable, or set the trigger

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: `enable` makes the playbook fire on its trigger for every matching container; `disable --cancel-runs` also stops running instances; `trigger` changes when it fires. Preview with `splunkctl soar playbooks enable 10`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar playbooks get 10 --json`.

```bash
splunkctl soar playbooks enable 10 --yes
splunkctl soar playbooks disable 10 --yes
splunkctl soar playbooks disable 10 --cancel-runs --yes
splunkctl soar playbooks trigger 10 --on artifact_created --yes
splunkctl soar playbooks trigger 10 --on container_resolved --yes
```

Expected result: `enable` sets `active: true`, `disable` sets `active: false`. Playbooks in `draft_mode: true` cannot be activated; the CLI adds a hint when the server rejects the enable. Re-import without `draft_mode` or finalize it in the Visual Playbook Editor first. `artifact_created` fires when an artifact is added, `container_resolved` on resolution. The `label` trigger seen in playbook metadata is import-only; the REST endpoint rejects setting it ("playbook_trigger is set to an invalid enum"), so it is not an accepted `--on` value.

#### Export a playbook

```bash
splunkctl soar playbooks export 10 > playbook.tgz
splunkctl soar playbooks export 10 --out ./exports/
splunkctl soar playbooks export 10 --unpack --out ./pb/
splunkctl soar playbooks export my_playbook --unpack --out ./pb/
```

Expected result: the bundle from `GET /rest/playbook/<id>/export`, written raw to stdout or as a tgz under `--out`; `--unpack` extracts `<name>.json` and `<name>.py` into the directory. A non-numeric identifier is looked up by exact scoped name (`<dir>/<module>`) first, then as a suffix match on the bare module name (`export my_playbook` finds `my-repo-dir/my_playbook`). Ambiguous or missing names return an error.

#### Import a playbook

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the playbook is created in `--scm` (default `local`) or, with the default `--force`, overwrites the existing one of the same name. Preview with `splunkctl soar playbooks import ./my_playbook/`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar playbooks list --json | jq '.[] | select(.name=="my_playbook")'`.

```bash
splunkctl soar playbooks import ./my_playbook/ --yes
splunkctl soar playbooks import ./my_playbook.tgz --yes
splunkctl soar playbooks import ./pb/ --scm my_repo --yes
splunkctl soar playbooks import ./pb/ --no-force --yes
```

Expected result: a directory is packed into a tgz on the fly; the payload is base64-encoded and posted to `/rest/import_playbook` as `{playbook, scm, force}`. `--no-force` refuses to overwrite.

#### Keep playbooks as code

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: step 5 overwrites the playbook on the instance with the edited bundle. Preview with step 4 (no `--yes`), apply with step 5, and verify with step 6.

```bash
splunkctl soar playbooks export my_playbook --unpack --out ./pb/
$EDITOR ./pb/my_playbook/my_playbook.py
cd ./pb && git add . && git commit -m "Update playbook logic" && cd ..
splunkctl soar playbooks import ./pb/my_playbook/
splunkctl soar playbooks import ./pb/my_playbook/ --yes
splunkctl soar playbooks list --json | jq '.[] | select(.name=="my_playbook")'
```

Expected result: the export and import pair gives a full as-code loop. Keep hand edits to the Python between the `## Custom Code Start` and `## Custom Code End` markers so the Visual Playbook Editor keeps them. [Manage configuration as code](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/state.md) pulls and pushes every playbook as the `soar-playbooks` type.

#### Delete playbooks

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the playbooks are removed irreversibly. Preview with `splunkctl soar playbooks delete local/old_pb` (the preview lists the identifiers as typed and needs no connectivity), apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar playbooks list`.

```bash
splunkctl soar playbooks export 10 --out ./backup/
splunkctl soar playbooks delete 10 --yes
splunkctl soar playbooks delete local/old_pb --yes
splunkctl soar playbooks delete 10 11 12 --yes
```

Expected result: `DELETE /rest/playbook/<id>` returns 405 and a POST with `{"delete": true}` reports success without removing anything on SOAR 8.5, so the command uses the browser's route: a Django Web UI login (CSRF cookie) followed by `POST /playbooks` with `{ids, delete: true}`. Because deletion is irreversible, names never suffix-match: pass the exact scoped name (`<dir>/<module>`) or the numeric id; a bare module name that only matches as a suffix returns a did-you-mean error carrying the full name and id. Name resolution happens at apply time. The command prints the server's per-playbook change and error report and exits 1 if any deletion failed.

#### List and sync SCM repositories

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: `sync` pulls and force-syncs the repo from its remote, replacing playbooks on the instance with the remote's versions. Preview with `splunkctl soar playbooks sync 1`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar playbooks list --repo <NAME>`.

```bash
splunkctl soar playbooks repos
splunkctl soar playbooks sync 1 --yes
```

Expected result: `repos` lists SCM repositories from `GET /rest/scm` (the lab ships one `local` repo at `file:////opt/phantom/scm/git/local`). `sync` posts to `/rest/scm/<id>` and is meant for HTTPS or SSH repos with a real remote. The built-in local repo has no remote, so the server rejects the sync with HTTP 400 "Remote named 'origin' didn't exist" on SOAR 8.5 (older versions return 500 "Operation not supported"); that is expected. Use `import` for local deployment.

### Troubleshooting

- `not_found` on `run` or `export` by name: no playbook matches; list with `splunkctl soar playbooks list` and use the id or the scoped `<dir>/<module>` name.
- `http` error on `enable` with the draft_mode hint: the playbook is a draft; re-import it without `draft_mode` or finalize it in the Visual Playbook Editor.
- `auth` on `delete` while everything else works: the profile has only an automation token; add a username and password with `splunkctl config init --soar`.
- Did-you-mean error on `delete`: you passed a bare module name; repeat the command with the full scoped name or id from the message.
- `http` 400 "Remote named 'origin' didn't exist" on `sync`: the repo is the local one; use `import`.
- `run --wait` exits 1: the run ended `failed` or `cancelled`, or `--timeout` elapsed; read `splunkctl soar playbooks runs get <RUN_ID> --blocks`.
- `http` 400 "playbook_trigger is set to an invalid enum": `--on label` is not supported; set the label in the playbook JSON and import it.

### See also

- [Work SOAR incidents](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-incidents.md)
- [Run actions](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-actions.md)
- [Manage custom functions](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-functions.md)
- [Handle approvals](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-approvals.md)
- [Manage configuration as code](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/state.md)
- [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)
- [Command reference: soar](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/soar.md)

## Run actions

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-actions.md


When to use: you want to run one app action (for example `lookup domain` or `block ip`) on one or more SOAR assets inside a container, wait for the result, read the per-asset output of a past run, or cancel a run that is stuck.

### Prerequisites

- SOAR credentials in the active profile and a passing `splunkctl soar test` (see [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)).
- A configured asset for the app whose action you want to run (`splunkctl soar assets list`, see [Configure assets and monitor ingestion](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-assets.md)).
- A container id to attach the run to (`splunkctl soar containers list`).
- A community license caps action runs at 100 per day; check `splunkctl soar license` (`max_allowed_actions_per_day`) before a bulk run.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl soar actions list [--container CONTAINER_ID] [--limit N] [--offset N]
splunkctl soar actions status <ACTION_RUN_ID>
splunkctl soar actions results <ACTION_RUN_ID>
splunkctl soar actions run --action <NAME> --asset <ASSET>... --container <CONTAINER_ID> [--param KEY=VALUE]... [--app APP_ID] [--type TYPE] [--name TEXT] [--wait] [--timeout SECONDS] [--yes]
splunkctl soar actions cancel <ACTION_RUN_ID> [--yes]
```

### Workflow

#### List past action runs

```bash
splunkctl soar actions list
splunkctl soar actions list --container 42
splunkctl soar actions list --limit 20 --offset 20
```

Expected result: one row per action run, newest first. `--offset` requires `--limit` and must be a multiple of it.

#### Run an action

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the app contacts the external system behind the asset (a DNS resolver, a firewall, an EDR) and the result lands on the container; a containment action changes that system. Preview with `splunkctl soar actions run --action "lookup domain" --asset google_dns --container 42 --param domain=example.com` and read the exact `/rest/action_run` JSON payload, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar actions status <ACTION_RUN_ID>`.

```bash
splunkctl soar actions run \
    --action "lookup domain" \
    --asset google_dns \
    --container 42 \
    --param domain=example.com
splunkctl soar actions run \
    --action "lookup domain" \
    --asset google_dns \
    --container 42 \
    --param domain=example.com --yes
```

Expected result: the dry run prints the payload; with `--yes` the run is created and its id printed. The CLI resolves each asset's `app_id` from the asset record and groups assets that share an `app_id` into one target entry. `--type` defaults to `investigate`; `--name` defaults to the action name.

#### Target several assets or pass several parameters

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the action runs on every asset listed, so a containment action reaches several systems at once. Preview by dropping `--yes`, apply by adding it back, and verify with `splunkctl soar actions results <ACTION_RUN_ID>`.

```bash
splunkctl soar actions run \
    --action "lookup domain" \
    --asset google_dns --asset custom_dns \
    --container 42 \
    --param domain=example.com --param type=A --yes
```

Expected result: one action run with both assets. Repeat `--asset` and `--param` as needed.

#### Skip the asset lookup with an explicit app id

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the action runs under the app id you pass with no check that it matches the asset. Preview by dropping `--yes`, apply by adding it back, and verify with `splunkctl soar actions status <ACTION_RUN_ID>`.

```bash
splunkctl soar actions run \
    --action "lookup domain" \
    --asset google_dns --app 55 \
    --container 42 \
    --param domain=example.com --yes
```

Expected result: the same run without the `/rest/asset` lookup; use it when you already know the app id.

#### Wait for completion

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the same action run as above; `--wait` only changes when the command returns. Preview by dropping `--yes`, apply by adding it back, and verify from the rendered `app_runs` detail or `splunkctl soar actions results <ACTION_RUN_ID>`.

```bash
splunkctl soar actions run \
    --action "lookup domain" \
    --asset google_dns \
    --container 42 \
    --param domain=example.com \
    --wait --timeout 120 --yes
```

Expected result: `--wait` polls `GET /rest/action_run/<id>` until the status reaches `success`, `failed`, or `cancelled`, then fetches the per-asset results (`app_runs`). The default timeout is 300 seconds. On success the command exits 0 and renders the `app_runs` detail; on failure or timeout it exits 1 with diagnostics.

#### Inspect a run

```bash
splunkctl soar actions status 999
splunkctl soar actions results 999
splunkctl soar actions results 999 --json | jq '.[].result_data[].data'
```

Expected result: `status` shows the run's state; `results` shows the `app_runs` detail, whose `result_data` holds the action output per asset, ready for `jq`.

#### Cancel a run

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the running action is stopped and its result never lands. Preview with `splunkctl soar actions cancel 999`, apply with `splunkctl soar actions cancel 999 --yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar actions status 999` (expect `cancelled`).

```bash
splunkctl soar actions cancel 999
splunkctl soar actions cancel 999 --yes
```

### Troubleshooting

- `not_found` for an asset name on `run`: the name must match `splunkctl soar assets list` exactly, or pass `--app <APP_ID>` to skip the lookup.
- `not_found` on `status` or `results`: the action run id does not exist; find it with `splunkctl soar actions list --container <ID>`.
- Exit 1 after `--wait`: the run finished `failed` or the timeout elapsed; read `splunkctl soar actions results <ID>` for the app's message, or raise `--timeout`.
- `run` is rejected after many runs in one day: the community license limit of 100 action runs per day may be spent; check `splunkctl soar license`.
- `--offset` rejected on `list`: it must be a multiple of `--limit`.
- `auth` or `permission` on `run` while `list` works: the credential's role cannot run actions; check its roles with `splunkctl soar users get <USER_ID>`.

### See also

- [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)
- [Configure assets and monitor ingestion](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-assets.md)
- [Work SOAR incidents](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-incidents.md)
- [Run playbooks](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-playbooks.md)
- [Look up indicators and evidence](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-indicators.md)
- [Command reference: soar](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/soar.md)

## Manage custom functions

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-functions.md


When to use: your playbooks call a SOAR custom function (a reusable Python snippet) and you want to back it up, deploy it from a repository, replace its source with a reviewed change, or remove it.

### Prerequisites

- SOAR credentials in the active profile and a passing `splunkctl soar test` (see [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)).
- At least one SCM repository on the instance (`splunkctl soar playbooks repos`); the lab ships a `local` repo. `update` needs it to resolve the repo id through `GET /rest/scm`.
- Username and password credentials for `delete`; SOAR refuses automation tokens on DELETE endpoints.
- For `import`: a `.tgz` in SOAR's export format, or a directory holding the paired `<name>.json` (metadata: name, module, description, parameters, outputs, python_version) and `<name>.py` (the function body). This is the same pair shape playbooks use under `custom_functions/`.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl soar functions list [--limit N] [--offset N]
splunkctl soar functions get <FUNCTION_ID>
splunkctl soar functions export <FUNCTION_ID> [--out FILE.tgz]
splunkctl soar functions import <PATH.tgz | DIR/> [--yes]
splunkctl soar functions update <FUNCTION_ID> --python <FILE.py> --message <TEXT> [--yes]
splunkctl soar functions delete <FUNCTION_ID> [--yes]
```

### Workflow

#### List and inspect functions

```bash
splunkctl soar functions list
splunkctl soar functions list --limit 10 --offset 0
splunkctl soar functions get 42
splunkctl soar functions get 42 --json
```

Expected result: one row per custom function; `get --json` includes the Python source.

#### Back up a function

```bash
splunkctl soar functions export 42 --out function.tgz
splunkctl soar functions export 42 > function.tgz
```

Expected result: a tgz (`GET /rest/custom_function/<id>/export`, served as `application/x-gzip`) containing the paired `.json` and `.py` files. Export before `update` or `delete` so you can import the previous version.

#### Import a function

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the function is created, or overwritten when one with the same name exists, because the import posts with `force: true`; playbooks pick up the new code on their next run. Preview with `splunkctl soar functions import ./my_function.tgz`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar functions list`.

```bash
splunkctl soar functions import ./my_function.tgz
splunkctl soar functions import ./my_function.tgz --yes
splunkctl soar functions import ./my_function/ --yes
```

Expected result: a directory is packed into a tgz automatically; the archive is base64-encoded and posted to `/rest/import_custom_function` with `scm: "local"` and `force: true`. Functions that fail validation are saved as drafts.

#### Replace the Python source

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the function body changes for every playbook that calls it; there is no server-side rollback except your export. Preview with `splunkctl soar functions update 42 --python ./updated_logic.py --message "Fix edge case in IP formatting"`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar functions get 42 --json`.

```bash
splunkctl soar functions export 42 --out before.tgz
splunkctl soar functions update 42 \
    --python ./updated_logic.py \
    --message "Fix edge case in IP formatting" --yes
```

Expected result: the CLI resolves the SCM repo id through `GET /rest/scm`, fetches the existing record, and posts only the changed fields (`python`, `commit_message`, `scm_id`). Functions imported as Python 2.7 are upgraded to Python 3 on update, because SOAR 8.x refuses to edit Python 2.7 functions. A function saved as a draft on import may leave draft mode once the new source passes validation, depending on its signature.

#### Delete a function

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the function is removed and playbooks that call it fail on their next run. Preview with `splunkctl soar functions delete 42`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar functions list`.

```bash
splunkctl soar functions export 42 --out before.tgz
splunkctl soar functions delete 42 --yes
```

Expected result: a DELETE that succeeds only with username and password credentials in the profile.

### Troubleshooting

- `not_found` on `get`, `export`, `update`, or `delete`: commands take the numeric id from `splunkctl soar functions list`, not the name.
- `update` exits 1 before posting with a message about SCM: the instance has no SCM repository; add one in the SOAR UI or check `splunkctl soar playbooks repos`.
- `auth` on `delete` while reads work: the profile is token-only; add a username and password with `splunkctl config init --soar`.
- `import` reports the function as a draft: validation failed; fix the `.json` metadata or the source and import again with `--yes`.
- `http` error on `import` about the archive: check that the directory or tgz holds the paired `<name>.json` and `<name>.py` with matching names.

### See also

- [Run playbooks](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-playbooks.md)
- [Maintain custom lists](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-lists.md)
- [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)
- [Command reference: soar](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/soar.md)

## Manage cases and workbooks

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-cases.md


When to use: an event needs formal incident handling, so you promote its container to a case with a workbook template, then work the phases and tasks (assign owners, mark progress, add closing notes) and maintain the templates themselves.

### Prerequisites

- SOAR credentials in the active profile and a passing `splunkctl soar test` (see [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)).
- Username and password credentials for `workbook-templates delete`; SOAR refuses automation tokens on most DELETE endpoints.
- A container id (`splunkctl soar containers list`). Cases are containers with `container_type=case` and an attached workbook of phases and tasks.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl soar cases promote <CONTAINER_ID> [--template NAME_OR_ID] [--yes]
splunkctl soar cases workbook <CONTAINER_ID>
splunkctl soar cases phase add --container <CONTAINER_ID> --name <NAME> [--order N] [--yes]
splunkctl soar cases task add --phase-id <PHASE_ID> --name <NAME> [--description TEXT] [--order N] [--yes]
splunkctl soar cases task update <TASK_ID> [--status incomplete|in_progress|complete] [--owner USER] [--note TEXT] [--yes]

splunkctl soar workbook-templates list [--limit N]
splunkctl soar workbook-templates get <NAME_OR_ID>
splunkctl soar workbook-templates create --name <NAME> --phases <"P1,P2,P3"> [--yes]
splunkctl soar workbook-templates update <NAME_OR_ID> --add-phase <NAME>... [--yes]
splunkctl soar workbook-templates delete <NAME_OR_ID> [--yes]
```

### Workflow

#### Pick a workbook template

```bash
splunkctl soar workbook-templates list
splunkctl soar workbook-templates list --limit 5 --json
splunkctl soar workbook-templates get "NIST 800-61"
splunkctl soar workbook-templates get 1 --json
```

Expected result: the preloaded templates with their phases. The default on most instances is NIST 800-61 (5 phases, 19 tasks). Numeric arguments are treated as ids; non-numeric arguments trigger a case-sensitive name lookup.

#### Promote a container to a case

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the container's type becomes `case` and every phase and task from the template is instantiated on it in one atomic POST to `/rest/container/<id>`. Preview with `splunkctl soar cases promote 42 --template "NIST 800-61"`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar cases workbook 42`.

```bash
splunkctl soar cases promote 42 --yes
splunkctl soar cases promote 42 --template "NIST 800-61" --yes
splunkctl soar cases promote 42 --template 3 --yes
```

Expected result: without `--template` the server's default template (`is_default=true`) is used; if no default exists the command errors and lists the available templates. `--template` accepts a case-sensitive name or a numeric id.

#### View the workbook

```bash
splunkctl soar cases workbook 42
splunkctl soar cases workbook 42 --json
```

Expected result: all phases (`/rest/container/<id>/phases`) with their nested tasks. Each task shows `status` (0 incomplete, 1 in_progress, 2 complete), owner, description, and notes.

#### Add a phase or a task

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: a new phase or task appears on the case's workbook for every analyst. Preview with `splunkctl soar cases phase add --container 42 --name "Recovery"`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar cases workbook 42`.

```bash
splunkctl soar cases phase add --container 42 --name "Recovery" --yes
splunkctl soar cases phase add --container 42 --name "Recovery" --order 3 --yes
splunkctl soar cases task add --phase-id 13 --name "Review logs" --yes
splunkctl soar cases task add --phase-id 13 --name "Review logs" \
    --description "Check all relevant logs" --order 5 --yes
```

Expected result: `phase add` posts `container_id`, `name`, and optional `order` to `/rest/workbook_phase`; `task add` posts to `/rest/workbook_task` with `phase_id` (the field is `phase_id`, not `phase`). Take the phase id from `cases workbook`.

#### Update a task

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the task's status, owner, or notes change on the live case. Preview with `splunkctl soar cases task update 100 --status complete`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar cases workbook 42`.

```bash
splunkctl soar cases task update 100 --status complete --yes
splunkctl soar cases task update 100 --status incomplete --yes
splunkctl soar cases task update 100 --status in_progress \
    --note "Reopening for active investigation" --yes
splunkctl soar cases task update 100 --owner analyst --yes
splunkctl soar cases task update 100 --status in_progress \
    --owner analyst --note "Taking over investigation" --yes
splunkctl soar cases task update 100 --note "Checked proxy logs, nothing found" --yes
```

Expected result: `--status` takes a name and the CLI maps it to the integer code SOAR expects:

| Name | Integer | Note required |
|---|---|---|
| `incomplete` | 0 | No |
| `in_progress` | 1 | Yes |
| `complete` | 2 | No |

The server allows only the transitions 0 to 2 (complete) and 2 to 1 (reopen as in progress); 0 to 1 is rejected with "Invalid status transition", so complete the task first. The `in_progress` transition also requires a closing note, which the CLI enforces client-side with a clear error before any API call. When `--note` accompanies `--status`, the note is sent inline in the task POST (field `note`), because the server rejects note-requiring transitions otherwise; the inline note still lands as a regular task note. A `--note` without `--status` posts to `/rest/note` with `task_id` set, and the task's `container_id` is resolved automatically with a GET on the task.

#### Create or extend a template

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: a new or changed template is offered to every future `promote`; existing cases are not touched. Preview with `splunkctl soar workbook-templates create --name "IR Workflow" --phases "Detect,Contain,Eradicate,Recover"`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar workbook-templates get "IR Workflow"`.

```bash
splunkctl soar workbook-templates create \
    --name "IR Workflow" --phases "Detect,Contain,Eradicate,Recover" --yes
splunkctl soar workbook-templates update "NIST 800-61" --add-phase "Lessons Learned" --yes
splunkctl soar workbook-templates update 2 --add-phase Eradicate --add-phase Recover --yes
```

Expected result: `create` makes phases in the order given, numbered from 1, and needs at least one phase. `update` appends new phases after the highest existing order value.

#### Delete a template

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the template is removed and can no longer be applied; cases already promoted keep their phases. Preview with `splunkctl soar workbook-templates delete "Custom Investigation"`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar workbook-templates list`.

```bash
splunkctl soar workbook-templates delete "Custom Investigation" --yes
splunkctl soar workbook-templates delete 3 --yes
```

Expected result: a `DELETE /rest/workbook_template/<id>`, which requires username and password credentials in the profile.

### Troubleshooting

- `not_found` on `promote --template` or `workbook-templates get`: names are case-sensitive; copy the exact name from `workbook-templates list` or use the id.
- `promote` fails with a list of templates: the instance has no default template; pass `--template`.
- Usage error "requires a closing note" on `task update --status in_progress`: add `--note "<reason>"`.
- `http` error "Invalid status transition": you tried 0 to 1; run `--status complete` first, then `--status in_progress --note ...`.
- `auth` on `workbook-templates delete` while reads work: the profile is token-only; add a username and password with `splunkctl config init --soar`.
- `not_found` on `task add`: `--phase-id` is the phase id from `cases workbook`, not the container id.

### See also

- [Work SOAR incidents](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-incidents.md)
- [Run playbooks](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-playbooks.md)
- [Handle approvals](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-approvals.md)
- [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)
- [Command reference: soar](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/soar.md)

## Handle approvals

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-approvals.md


When to use: a playbook has paused at a prompt block and is waiting for a human decision, and you want to review and approve or deny it from the terminal instead of the SOAR UI, so automation can continue.

### Prerequisites

- SOAR credentials in the active profile and a passing `splunkctl soar test` (see [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)).
- A playbook that contains a prompt block (a manual or automated prompt action). When such a playbook runs and reaches that block it creates an approval request tied to the container and pauses; the approval stays `pending` until someone responds through the UI or the REST API (`/rest/external_prompt/<id>`), then the playbook resumes along the approve or deny branch.
- Without active playbooks that contain prompt blocks the approval list is empty; that is normal on a fresh or lab instance.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl soar approvals list [--pending] [--container CONTAINER_ID]
splunkctl soar approvals get <APPROVAL_ID>
splunkctl soar approvals respond <APPROVAL_ID> <approve|deny> [--message TEXT] [--yes]
```

### Workflow

#### Find pending approvals

```bash
splunkctl soar approvals list
splunkctl soar approvals list --pending
splunkctl soar approvals list --container 42
splunkctl soar approvals list --container 42 --pending
splunkctl soar approvals list --json
```

Expected result: one row per approval. `--pending` adds a `_filter_status="pending"` filter so only unanswered approvals return. `--container` queries the per-container endpoint (`/rest/container/<id>/approvals`) instead of the global collection. Both flags compose. An empty result exits 0 with clean output (`[]` in JSON mode, `No approvals found.` in table mode).

#### Read one approval

```bash
splunkctl soar approvals get 5
splunkctl soar approvals get 5 --json
```

Expected result: the detail summary view (`/rest/approval/<id>?_detail=detail_summary_view`): the full approval object including message, status, and response history.

#### Approve or deny

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile; the dry-run banner names it so you never answer a prompt on the wrong instance. Impact: the paused playbook resumes along the chosen branch, which may run containment actions. Preview with `splunkctl soar approvals respond 5 approve --message "Verified IOC"` (the preview shows the approval id, action, and message), apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar containers get 42 --playbook-runs`.

```bash
splunkctl soar approvals respond 5 approve
splunkctl soar approvals respond 5 approve --message "Verified IOC" --yes
splunkctl soar approvals respond 5 deny --message "Insufficient evidence" --yes
```

Expected result: a POST to `/rest/external_prompt/<id>` with `{status: "approve"|"deny"}` and the optional message, and the playbook run moves past the prompt. The action argument accepts only `approve` or `deny` (case-insensitive); any other value is a usage error before any API call.

#### Run the full cycle

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: step 3 resumes the paused playbook. Preview with `splunkctl soar approvals respond 5 approve --message "Verified IOC"`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with step 4.

```bash
splunkctl soar approvals list --pending
splunkctl soar approvals get 5
splunkctl soar approvals respond 5 approve --message "Verified IOC" --yes
splunkctl soar containers get 42 --playbook-runs
```

Expected result: the approval leaves the pending list and the container's playbook run shows progress past the prompt block.

### Troubleshooting

- `not_found` on `get` or `respond` (`{"error": {"kind": "not_found", "http_status": 404, ...}}`, exit 1): the approval id is wrong or was deleted with its container; list again with `--pending`.
- `conflict` on `respond`: the approval was already answered in the UI or by someone else; `get` shows the recorded decision.
- Usage error (exit 2) on `respond`: the action must be `approve` or `deny`.
- `permission` on `respond` while `list` works: the account's role cannot answer prompts; respond with a user whose role may.
- The playbook did not resume after approval: check `splunkctl soar playbooks runs list --container 42 --status failed`; a failure in the next block looks like a stuck approval from the queue.

### See also

- [Run playbooks](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-playbooks.md)
- [Work SOAR incidents](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-incidents.md)
- [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)
- [Command reference: soar](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/soar.md)

## Maintain custom lists

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-lists.md


When to use: your playbooks read a SOAR custom list (an allowlist, blocklist, or lookup table) and you need to add or remove rows, replace the whole list from a file, or back it up as JSON or CSV.

### Prerequisites

- SOAR credentials in the active profile and a passing `splunkctl soar test` (see [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)).
- For `create`, `update`, and `import`: a JSON or CSV file with at least one row (formats below).
- `delete` works with an automation token; `decided_list` is the one SOAR DELETE endpoint that accepts token auth.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl soar lists list [--limit N]
splunkctl soar lists get <NAME_OR_ID>
splunkctl soar lists create --name <NAME> --file <ROWS.json|ROWS.csv> [--yes]
splunkctl soar lists update <NAME_OR_ID> --file <ROWS.json|ROWS.csv> [--yes]
splunkctl soar lists add-row <NAME_OR_ID> --values <"a,b,c" | '["a, b","c"]'> [--yes]
splunkctl soar lists remove-row <NAME_OR_ID> --index <N> [--yes]
splunkctl soar lists export <NAME_OR_ID> [--format json|csv] [--out FILE]
splunkctl soar lists import --name <NAME> --file <ROWS.json|ROWS.csv> [--yes]
splunkctl soar lists delete <NAME_OR_ID> [--yes]
```

`get`, `update`, `add-row`, `remove-row`, `export`, and `delete` accept a numeric id or a list name; names are resolved through a `_filter_name` query.

### Workflow

#### Read a list

```bash
splunkctl soar lists list
splunkctl soar lists get blocklist
splunkctl soar lists get 42 --json
```

Expected result: list metadata plus its rows. Content is an array of rows, each row an array of strings; SOAR does not distinguish a header row from data.

#### Back up a list

```bash
splunkctl soar lists export blocklist --out backup.json
splunkctl soar lists export blocklist --format csv --out backup.csv
```

JSON export writes the content array only. CSV uses SOAR's `formatted_content` route. Export before any `update` or `import` so you can restore the previous rows.

#### Create a list from a file

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: a new custom list that playbooks can read immediately. Preview with `splunkctl soar lists create --name my_list --file rows.json`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar lists get my_list`.

```bash
splunkctl soar lists create --name my_list --file rows.json
splunkctl soar lists create --name my_list --file rows.json --yes
splunkctl soar lists create --name my_list --file data.csv --yes
```

JSON input is an array of arrays:

```json
[
  ["header1", "header2"],
  ["value1", "value2"],
  ["value3", "value4"]
]
```

CSV input is parsed client side into the same shape; the header row becomes the first row:

```csv
header1,header2
value1,value2
value3,value4
```

The SOAR API rejects `text/csv`, so all content is sent as JSON.

#### Add or remove one row

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the CLI fetches the current rows, changes one, and posts the full list back; rows changed in the UI between fetch and post are overwritten. Preview with `splunkctl soar lists add-row my_list --values "val1,val2,val3"`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar lists get my_list`.

```bash
splunkctl soar lists add-row my_list --values "val1,val2,val3" --yes
splunkctl soar lists add-row my_list --values '["val, with comma","val2"]' --yes
splunkctl soar lists remove-row my_list --index 2 --yes
```

`--values` takes comma-separated values, or a JSON array when a value contains a comma. `--index` is 0-based within the content array, so the header row is index 0.

#### Replace a whole list

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: every existing row is overwritten; there is no merge. Preview with `splunkctl soar lists update my_list --file new_rows.json` and read the row count in the preview, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar lists get my_list`.

```bash
splunkctl soar lists export my_list --out before.json
splunkctl soar lists update my_list --file new_rows.json
splunkctl soar lists update my_list --file new_rows.json --yes
```

#### Import from a repository

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the list is created if it does not exist, otherwise fully replaced. Preview with `splunkctl soar lists import --name my_list --file rows.json`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar lists get my_list`.

```bash
splunkctl soar lists import --name my_list --file rows.json
splunkctl soar lists import --name my_list --file data.csv --yes
```

`import` is the command to use from CI, because it is idempotent for a given file.

#### Delete a list

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the list is removed and playbooks that read it start failing. Preview with `splunkctl soar lists delete blocklist`, apply with `splunkctl soar lists delete blocklist --yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar lists list`.

```bash
splunkctl soar lists export blocklist --out blocklist.json
splunkctl soar lists delete blocklist
splunkctl soar lists delete 42 --yes
```

### Troubleshooting

- `not_found` by name: run `splunkctl soar lists list` and check the exact name, or use the id.
- `create` rejects the file: it needs at least one row, and JSON must be an array of arrays of strings.
- A value with a comma was split in `add-row`: pass `--values` as a JSON array.
- Rows disappeared after `update`: `update` is a full replace; restore from your export with `splunkctl soar lists update <NAME> --file before.json --yes`.

### See also

- [Run playbooks](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-playbooks.md)
- [Look up indicators and evidence](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-indicators.md)
- [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)
- [Command reference: soar](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/soar.md)

## Look up indicators and evidence

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-indicators.md


When to use: you have an IP, domain, hash, or URL and want to know where SOAR has seen it before, or you are building a case and need to tag artifacts, notes, or action runs on a container as formal evidence.

### Prerequisites

- SOAR credentials in the active profile and a passing `splunkctl soar test` (see [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)).
- For the `indicators` commands (`list`, `get`, `pivot`, `stats`): the `use_indicators` feature flag enabled on the instance. It is off by default on new installs; enable it in Administration > Product Settings > Feature Toggles, or `POST /rest/feature_flag` with `name='use_indicators'` and `value=true`.
- Username and password credentials for `evidence remove`; SOAR refuses automation tokens on DELETE.
- The `evidence` commands work regardless of the indicators flag.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl soar indicators list [--type ip|domain|hash|url|email|file|process|vault_id] [--limit N]
splunkctl soar indicators get <VALUE>
splunkctl soar indicators pivot <VALUE>
splunkctl soar indicators stats

splunkctl soar evidence list --container <CONTAINER_ID>
splunkctl soar evidence add <CONTAINER_ID> --object <artifact|note|action_run> --id <OBJECT_ID> [--yes]
splunkctl soar evidence remove <EVIDENCE_ID> [--yes]
```

### Workflow

#### Confirm the indicators feature is on

```bash
splunkctl soar indicators stats
```

Expected result: aggregated breakdowns by type and severity (`indicator_stats_type` and `indicator_stats_severity`). Every indicator command first checks `/rest/feature_flag` for `use_indicators=true`; if the flag is off or the endpoint is unreachable the command exits 1 with:

```text
Error: Indicators feature is disabled on this SOAR instance.
Enable it in Administration > Product Settings > Feature Toggles,
or POST /rest/feature_flag with name='use_indicators' and value=true.
```

#### List indicators

```bash
splunkctl soar indicators list
splunkctl soar indicators list --type ip
splunkctl soar indicators list --limit 20
splunkctl soar indicators list --json
```

Expected result: one row per indicator from `GET /rest/indicator`, optionally filtered to one `--type` (`ip`, `domain`, `hash`, `url`, `email`, `file`, `process`, `vault_id`).

#### Look up one value

```bash
splunkctl soar indicators get 8.8.8.8
splunkctl soar indicators get evil.com --json
```

Expected result: the indicator record for that exact value, through `GET /rest/indicator_by_value`.

#### Pivot to every container that saw it

```bash
splunkctl soar indicators pivot evil.com
splunkctl soar indicators pivot 8.8.8.8 --json
```

Expected result: every container where the IOC has appeared (`GET /rest/indicator_common_container`), answering "where else have we seen this IP?" for cross-case correlation.

#### List evidence on a container

```bash
splunkctl soar evidence list --container 100
splunkctl soar evidence list --container 100 --json
```

Expected result: the evidence items (`GET /rest/evidence`) linking artifacts, notes, or action runs to the container as formally tagged proof. `--container` is required.

#### Add evidence

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile; the dry-run banner shows the host and the payload. Impact: the object is tagged as evidence on the container and appears in case reports. Preview with `splunkctl soar evidence add 100 --object artifact --id 42`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar evidence list --container 100`.

```bash
splunkctl soar evidence add 100 --object artifact --id 42
splunkctl soar evidence add 100 --object artifact --id 42 --yes
splunkctl soar evidence add 100 --object note --id 7 --yes
splunkctl soar evidence add 100 --object action_run --id 999 --yes
```

Expected result: a `POST /rest/evidence` and a new evidence id. `--object` accepts `artifact`, `note`, or `action_run`; `--id` is that object's id, not the container id.

#### Remove evidence
