> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: the evidence tag is removed; the underlying artifact, note, or action run stays. Preview with `splunkctl soar evidence remove 5`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar evidence list --container 100`.

```bash
splunkctl soar evidence remove 5
splunkctl soar evidence remove 5 --yes
```

Expected result: a `DELETE /rest/evidence/<id>`, which needs username and password credentials; a token-only profile gets a clear `auth` error.

### Troubleshooting

- "Indicators feature is disabled" (exit 1): enable `use_indicators` as shown above, then rerun; the check runs before every indicators command.
- `not_found` on `indicators get`: the value must match exactly (no wildcards, no trailing dot on domains); list with `--type` to find the stored form.
- `auth` on `evidence remove` while `add` works: the profile is token-only; add a username and password with `splunkctl config init --soar`.
- `not_found` on `evidence add`: `--id` must be an existing artifact, note, or action run id, and it must belong to the container you name.
- `evidence remove` needs the evidence id, not the artifact id: take it from the `id` column of `evidence list`.

### See also

- [Work SOAR incidents](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-incidents.md)
- [Manage cases and workbooks](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-cases.md)
- [Run actions](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-actions.md)
- [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)
- [Command reference: soar](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/soar.md)

## Ingest SIEM results into SOAR

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-ingest.md


When to use: you have Splunk search results (ES notables, firewall hits, a hunting query) and want them in SOAR as containers and CEF artifacts so playbooks can act on them, with the official CIM-to-CEF mapping, deduplication, and a preview before anything is sent.

### Prerequisites

- A Splunk profile that passes `splunkctl doctor` and SOAR credentials that pass `splunkctl soar test` (see [Configure](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/configure.md) and [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)).
- A label that exists on the SOAR instance (`splunkctl soar meta labels`); the default is `events`.
- Either an SPL query (`--spl`) or the sid of a finished search job (`--sid`, from `splunkctl search jobs`); the two are mutually exclusive.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl soar ingest (--spl <SPL> | --sid <SID>) [--earliest TIME] [--latest TIME] [--app APP] [--label LABEL] [--severity NAME] [--sensitivity NAME] [--sdi-field FIELD] [--container-name TEXT] [--container-name-field FIELD] [--grouping] [--map CEF_KEY=SPLUNK_FIELD]... [--map-file FILE.yaml] [--include-unmapped] [--no-automation] [--yes]
```

Defaults: `--label events`, `--sensitivity amber`, `--sdi-field event_id`, severity derived from the row, one container per row.

### Workflow

#### Preview an ingest

```bash
splunkctl soar ingest --spl '| makeresults count=2 | eval src="10.0.0.1"'
splunkctl soar ingest --spl 'index=firewall src=10.0.0.1' --earliest -24h
```

Expected result: the dry run shows the container count and artifacts per container, the active CIM-to-CEF mapping table (first 10 entries), and a sample CEF payload from the first result row. No data is sent to SOAR. The search runs through the same machinery as `splunkctl search run`; `--earliest`, `--latest`, and `--app` scope it.

#### Apply the ingest

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile, with results read from the Splunk host in the same profile. Impact: new containers and artifacts are created and playbooks fire on the last artifact of each container. Preview with `splunkctl soar ingest --spl 'index=firewall src=10.0.0.1' --earliest -24h`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl soar containers list --label events --since <today>`.

```bash
splunkctl soar ingest --spl '| makeresults count=2 | eval src="10.0.0.1"' --yes
splunkctl soar ingest --sid 1720000000.42 --yes
splunkctl soar ingest --spl 'index=firewall' --label notable --severity high --sensitivity green --yes
```

Expected result: one container per result row (or one container for all rows with `--grouping`), each with CEF artifacts, and a summary of containers and artifacts created and skipped.

#### Control the field mapping

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: containers and artifacts are created with the mapped CEF keys. Preview by dropping `--yes` and reading the mapping table and sample CEF payload, apply by adding it back, and verify with `splunkctl soar artifacts list --container <CONTAINER_ID>`.

```bash
splunkctl soar ingest --spl 'index=firewall' --map sourceAddress=my_src --yes
splunkctl soar ingest --spl 'index=firewall' --map-file ~/.splunkctl/cim_cef_map.yaml --yes
splunkctl soar ingest --spl 'index=firewall' --include-unmapped --yes
```

Expected result: the built-in `CIM_CEF_MAP` mirrors the official Splunk SOAR Connector for Splunk mapping (with the upstream `butesIn` typo fixed to `bytesIn`). CEF keys get automatic `cef_types` from the built-in `CEF_CONTAINS_MAP` (for example `sourceAddress` becomes `["ip", "host name"]`), which makes artifact fields actionable as playbook inputs. `--map` overrides one key per flag; `--map-file` loads a YAML file:

```yaml
mappings:
  src: {cef: sourceAddress, contains: [ip]}
  custom_score: {cef: riskScore}
unmapped: drop   # or "pass" to keep unmapped fields as custom CEF keys
```

Fields not in the map are dropped by default. `--include-unmapped` (or `unmapped: pass`) passes them through as custom CEF keys; underscore-prefixed internal fields such as `_raw` and `_time` are always excluded.

#### Group rows into one container

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: one container with every row as an artifact is created. Preview by dropping `--yes`, apply by adding it back, and verify with `splunkctl soar containers list --label events --since <today>`.

```bash
splunkctl soar ingest --spl 'index=firewall src=10.0.0.1' --grouping --yes
```

Expected result: a single container with one artifact per row instead of one container per row.

#### Name containers and set severity

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: containers are created with the chosen names and severity, which drives SOAR queue sorting. Preview by dropping `--yes` and reading the container list in the dry run, apply by adding it back, and verify with `splunkctl soar containers list --severity high`.

```bash
splunkctl soar ingest --spl 'index=notable' --container-name-field rule_name --yes
splunkctl soar ingest --spl 'index=firewall' --container-name "Firewall sweep" --yes
splunkctl soar ingest --spl 'index=firewall' --severity high --yes
```

Expected result: the name is chosen in this order: `--container-name-field` (that row field's value), `--container-name` (a literal or template), the `rule_name` field (ES notable convention), then the fallback `"Splunk Log Entry on <_time>: <source>"`. Severity checks the row's `severity` first, then `urgency`, and defaults to `medium`; multivalue fields take the highest value, and `--severity` overrides:

| Splunk severity or urgency | SOAR severity |
|---|---|
| informational, low | low |
| medium | medium |
| high, critical | high |

#### Rerun safely with deduplication

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: only rows whose SDI is new become containers or artifacts; changing `--sdi-field` can make every row look new and duplicate the queue. Preview by dropping `--yes` and reading the skipped counts, apply by adding it back, and verify with `splunkctl soar containers list --filter '_filter_source_data_identifier="<SDI>"'`.

```bash
splunkctl soar ingest --spl 'index=notable | head 10' --yes
splunkctl soar ingest --spl 'index=notable | head 10' --yes
splunkctl soar ingest --spl 'index=firewall' --sdi-field event_hash --yes
```

Expected result: the second run reports the existing containers and artifacts and skips creating them. The source data identifier (SDI) is the `event_id` field when present, otherwise a SHA-256 hash of the full row; `--sdi-field` picks another field. Containers are prechecked client-side with `_filter_source_data_identifier`, and the server-side fallback returns `existing_container_id`. Artifacts are prechecked client-side only, because the server does not deduplicate artifacts.

#### Control playbook automation

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile. Impact: with `--no-automation` no playbook fires for the new artifacts; without it the last artifact per container triggers active playbooks. Preview by dropping `--yes`, apply by adding it back, and verify with `splunkctl soar playbooks runs list --container <CONTAINER_ID>`.

```bash
splunkctl soar ingest --spl 'index=firewall' --no-automation --yes
```

Expected result: by default every artifact is created with `run_automation: false` except the last artifact actually created in each container, which gets `run_automation: true`, so playbooks fire once the container is fully populated. `--no-automation` suppresses automation on all artifacts.

#### Ingest ES notables

> **Safety:** Target is the SOAR host in the active profile, reading notables from the Splunk host in the same profile. Impact: one container per notable with its context fields as CEF keys, and playbooks fire on each. Preview by dropping `--yes`, apply by adding it back, and verify with `splunkctl soar containers list --label events --since <today>`.

```bash
splunkctl soar ingest \
    --spl 'index=notable | head 10' \
    --include-unmapped --yes
```

Expected result: notables with their native fields: SDI from `event_id` (the default `--sdi-field`), the container name from `rule_name`, severity mapped from the notable's `severity` or `urgency`, and `--include-unmapped` preserving `event_id`, `risk_score`, `security_domain`, and other context fields as custom CEF keys for playbook use.

### Troubleshooting

- Usage error "No SOAR host configured": run `splunkctl config init --soar`.
- `confirmation_required` from the SIEM search: the SPL contains a write command; remove it, the ingest only reads results.
- `auth` or `connection` naming the Splunk host: the SIEM side failed; run `splunkctl doctor`. Naming the SOAR host: run `splunkctl soar test`.
- `not_found` on `--sid`: the job expired; rerun with `--spl`, or create a fresh job with `splunkctl search run ... --detach`.
- `http` error on container creation: the server rejected a field; check that `--label` exists (`splunkctl soar meta labels`) and `--severity` and `--sensitivity` are valid names (`splunkctl soar meta severities`).
- Everything is skipped on rerun: deduplication by SDI is working; change `--sdi-field` only if the rows are genuinely new.
- Playbooks did not fire: `--no-automation` was set, or the playbook's trigger and label do not match (see [Run playbooks](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-playbooks.md)).

### See also

- [Run searches](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/search.md)
- [Triage ES notables](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/es.md)
- [Work SOAR incidents](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-incidents.md)
- [Run playbooks](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-playbooks.md)
- [Configure assets and monitor ingestion](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-assets.md)
- [Command reference: soar](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/soar.md)

## Manage configuration as code

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/state.md


When to use: your change process needs an audit trail for detection content: pull a versioned snapshot of an instance, edit it like code, diff it against the live instance, then push with a before-and-after JSON report a change ticket can reference as evidence. `state` unifies the `rules` and `parsers` export and import loops with macros, lookups, dashboards, and the SOAR playbook, list, and asset types in one pull, edit, diff, push loop.

### Prerequisites

- A Splunk profile that passes `splunkctl doctor`; the account needs write access to every app you intend to push to.
- For `soar-playbooks`, `soar-lists`, and `soar-assets`: SOAR credentials in the profile (`splunkctl config init --soar` or `SOAR_HOST`). Mixed SIEM and SOAR types in one command work; each type is routed to its own client.
- The same `--app` scope (or none) on `pull`, `diff`, and `push` when lookups or dashboards are involved (see "Pull a snapshot").

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl state pull --dir <DIR> [--app APP] [--types rules,parsers,macros,lookups,dashboards,soar-playbooks,soar-lists,soar-assets]
splunkctl state diff --dir <DIR> [--app APP] [--types LIST]
splunkctl state push --dir <DIR> [--app APP] [--types LIST] [--report FILE.json] [--yes]
```

`--types` defaults to all eight types. `--app` is accepted by all three commands but ignored for SOAR types, which are not scoped by Splunk app.

### Workflow

#### Pull a snapshot

```bash
splunkctl state pull --dir ./snapshot
splunkctl state pull --dir ./snapshot --app my_app
splunkctl state pull --dir ./snapshot --types rules,macros
splunkctl state pull --dir ./snap --types soar-playbooks
splunkctl state pull --dir ./snap --types soar-lists,soar-assets
splunkctl state pull --dir ./snap --types rules,soar-playbooks
```

Expected result: a tree you can commit:

```text
snapshot/
  manifest.json       # tool version, host, per-type object counts
  rules.yml           # saved searches (rules_io's YAML shape)
  parsers.yml         # props/transforms stanzas with explicit keys
  macros.yml          # macros.conf stanzas with explicit keys
  lookups/<name>      # one CSV per lookup table file
  dashboards/<name>.xml  # one XML export per dashboard
  soar-playbooks/
    index.json                  # id/name/filename map for diff/push
    local__detect_malware.tgz   # one tgz per playbook (slash -> __)
  soar-lists/
    blocklist.json              # JSON array-of-arrays content
  soar-assets/
    firewall.json               # asset config (passwords masked)
```

`manifest.json` deliberately has no timestamp, only `version`, `host`, and `types` (object counts); a wall-clock stamp would make two pulls non-deterministic to diff, and the commit or file mtime already answers "when". `pull` owns and overwrites only the types it is asked for and is otherwise read-only against the instance.

Keep `--app` consistent across pull, diff, and push. `lookups/<name>` and `dashboards/<name>.xml` are a flat layout where the file name carries no app, unlike `rules.yml`, `parsers.yml`, and `macros.yml`, where every document records its own `app`. If you pull unscoped (or with one `--app`) and then diff or push with a different single `--app`, a lookup or dashboard from another app can be misattributed: it shows as `added` even though it exists live, and `push` would try to create it under the wrong app.

What each type supports:

| Type | Pull (read) | Diff | Push (apply) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rules` | `rules_io` export | field-level | `rules_io` import |
| `parsers` | `parsers_io` export (explicit keys) | key-level | `parsers_io` import |
| `macros` | explicit-key conf read | key-level | `conf_ops.set_keys` |
| `lookups` | CSV download | content hash | CSV upload or update |
| `dashboards` | XML export | content hash | not supported |
| `soar-playbooks` | tgz export | content hash (SHA-256 of the tgz bytes) | tgz import via `POST /rest/import_playbook` |
| `soar-lists` | JSON content export | content hash | create or full replace |
| `soar-assets` | JSON config export (password fields masked as `****`) | field-level, masked fields ignored | fetch-merge-post, masked values skipped so server secrets survive |

Every path reuses the per-type machinery (`rules_io`, `parsers_io`, `conf_ops`, `client.upload_lookup`, the SOAR commands); `state` is orchestration only, never a second implementation.

#### Edit the snapshot like code

```bash
git init ./snapshot && git -C ./snapshot add . && git -C ./snapshot commit -m "Baseline from prod"
$EDITOR ./snapshot/rules.yml
git -C ./snapshot commit -am "Raise brute force threshold to 30"
```

Expected result: every change is a reviewable commit. The YAML shapes are the ones `rules export` and `parsers export` write (see [Manage detection rules](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/rules.md) and [Manage source types and extractions](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/parsers.md)).

#### Diff against the live instance

```bash
splunkctl state diff --dir ./snapshot
splunkctl state diff --dir ./snapshot --types rules --json
splunkctl state diff --dir ./snap --types soar-lists
```

Expected result: every object in each type, not just deltas, classified as:

- `added`: on disk, not on the instance (`push` would create it)
- `removed`: on the instance, not on disk (`push` does not delete it)
- `modified`: both exist and differ; rules, parsers, macros, and SOAR assets carry a structured `fields: [{field, old, new}]` diff, while lookups, dashboards, playbooks, and lists (blob-shaped) carry a `sha256` before and after instead
- `unchanged`: both exist and match

```json
[
  {
    "type": "rules",
    "name": "Failed Logins",
    "change": "modified",
    "fields": [{"field": "search", "old": "index=old", "new": "index=new"}]
  }
]
```

`diff` always exits 0; it is a report, not a gate.

Dashboard drift is a raw-XML content hash, so `diff` can show a few dashboards as `modified` with zero real edits: Splunk's export is not always byte-identical across requests, and two apps sharing a dashboard name collide in the flat `dashboards/<name>.xml` layout. This is cosmetic, because dashboards are never pushed, but do not treat a non-empty dashboard diff as evidence of a real change without checking.

#### Preview the push and save the plan

```bash
splunkctl state push --dir ./snapshot
splunkctl state push --dir ./snapshot --types rules --report change-12345-plan.json
```

Expected result: exactly what `--yes` would create or update, nothing applied. `--report` writes `{host, types, changes, applied}` with `applied: false`; attach it to the change ticket for approval.

#### Apply the approved push

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host (and, for SOAR types, the SOAR host) in the active profile. Impact: every `added` object is created and every `modified` object is updated on the live instance; `removed` objects are never deleted. Preview with `splunkctl state push --dir ./snapshot --types rules --report change-12345-plan.json`, apply with `splunkctl state push --dir ./snapshot --types rules --yes --report change-12345-applied.json`, and verify with `splunkctl state diff --dir ./snapshot --types rules` (expect only `unchanged`).

```bash
splunkctl state push --dir ./snapshot --types rules --yes --report change-12345-applied.json
splunkctl state push --dir ./snap --types soar-assets --yes
splunkctl state diff --dir ./snapshot --types rules
```

Expected result: the report is written again with `applied: true` as the change record. `changes` has the same shape as `diff`'s modified and added rows plus `before` and `after` maps built from the field diff:

```json
{
  "host": "splunk.example.com:8089",
  "types": ["rules"],
  "changes": [
    {
      "type": "rules",
      "name": "Failed Logins",
      "change": "modified",
      "before": {"search": "index=old"},
      "after": {"search": "index=new"}
    }
  ],
  "applied": true
}
```

`changes` never includes `removed` or `unchanged` entries, only what was (or would be) created or updated. `removed` drift and dashboard apply-unsupported drift are console notes, not report entries, because neither is ever applied.

`push` never deletes. An instance object with no on-disk counterpart is classified `removed`, surfaced as a note (`note: rules: 2 object(s) on the instance only -- not deleted (push never deletes)`), and never touched; there is no delete path in `state push` by design. To remove something, use the type-specific `delete` command (`rules delete`, `lookups delete`, and so on) with its own guard.

Dashboards are pull and diff only. `state push` has no apply path for them: drifted dashboards are reported as apply-unsupported and skipped without erroring:

```text
note: dashboards: 1 drifted object(s), apply not supported (export-only, no import path)
```

If `dashboards` is the only `--types` value and nothing else drifted, `push` still exits 0 and, with `--report`, still writes an artifact with `changes: []`. To change a dashboard, use `splunkctl dashboards update` directly (see [Manage dashboards](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/dashboards.md)).

#### Run the change-ticket loop end to end

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: step 5 creates and updates every drifted rule on the instance. Preview with step 4 and attach its report to the ticket, apply with step 5 once approved, and verify with `splunkctl state diff --dir ./snapshot --types rules` (expect only `unchanged`).

```bash
splunkctl state pull --dir ./snapshot --types rules
$EDITOR ./snapshot/rules.yml
splunkctl state diff --dir ./snapshot --types rules
splunkctl state push --dir ./snapshot --types rules --report change-12345-plan.json
splunkctl state push --dir ./snapshot --types rules --yes --report change-12345-applied.json
```

Expected result: a plan artifact for approval and an applied artifact as the record, from the same file; the same JSON works as the dry-run attachment and as the evidence of what actually happened.

### Troubleshooting

- Usage error "No SOAR host configured" when a SOAR type is requested: run `splunkctl config init --soar` or set `SOAR_HOST`.
- A lookup or dashboard shows `added` although it exists: `--app` differs between `pull` and `diff` or `push`; rerun all three with the same scope.
- `permission` on `push`: the account cannot write to the app that owns the object; narrow the run with `--types` or `--app` and fix the role.
- `push` printed "not deleted (push never deletes)": expected; delete with the type's own `delete` command if that is intended.
- Dashboards appear `modified` on every `diff`: cosmetic hash drift (see "Diff against the live instance"); verify with `splunkctl dashboards get <NAME>` before acting.

### See also

- [Manage detection rules](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/rules.md)
- [Manage source types and extractions](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/parsers.md)
- [Manage macros, eventtypes, tags](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/knowledge.md)
- [Manage lookups](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/lookups.md)
- [Manage dashboards](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/dashboards.md)
- [Run playbooks](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-playbooks.md)
- [Maintain custom lists](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-lists.md)
- [Configure assets and monitor ingestion](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-assets.md)
- [Audit changes and attest RBAC](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/audit.md)
- [Command reference: state](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/state.md)

## Edit any conf file

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/conf.md


When to use: you need to read or change a stanza in a conf file that has no dedicated command group (`limits`, `authorize`, `server`, `web`, `savedsearches` keys the `rules` group does not expose, and anything else under `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/*/local`), and you want a field-level preview before the write.

### Prerequisites

- A profile that passes `splunkctl doctor` (see [Configure](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/configure.md)).
- An account allowed to edit the target conf file; sensitive files such as `authorize.conf` and `server.conf` need `admin_all_objects`.
- There is no blocklist: `conf` edits `authorize.conf`, `server.conf`, and `web.conf` as readily as `macros.conf`. The dry-run guard and `--yes` are the only safety net, so read the preview before applying to a sensitive file.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl conf files [--app APP] [--filter SUBSTRING] [--limit N] [--offset N]
splunkctl conf list <FILE> [--app APP] [--filter SUBSTRING] [--limit N] [--offset N]
splunkctl conf get <FILE> <STANZA> [--app APP] [--key KEY]
splunkctl conf set <FILE> <STANZA> <KEY=VALUE>... [--yes]
splunkctl conf unset <FILE> <STANZA> <KEY>... [--yes]
splunkctl conf reload <FILE> [--yes]
```

`FILE` is the conf name without `.conf` (`macros`, `limits`, `authorize`). `parsers` covers `props.conf` and `transforms.conf`, and `macros`, `eventtypes`, and `tags` have friendlier verbs (see [Manage macros, eventtypes, tags](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/knowledge.md)); `conf` reaches every file the same way, so nothing detection-relevant is locked out of code review or CI.

### Workflow

#### Find the right file and stanza

```bash
splunkctl conf files
splunkctl conf files --filter tag
splunkctl conf list macros
splunkctl conf list macros --app my_app
```

Expected result: the conf files the server knows, then the stanzas in one file. Pass `--app` on `list` and `files`: the unscoped default view can miss app-private stanzas, the same as `rules list` and `dashboards list`.

#### Read a stanza

```bash
splunkctl conf get macros my_macro
splunkctl conf get macros my_macro --key definition
splunkctl conf get eventtypes authentication --json | jq .
```

Expected result: every key in the stanza, or one key's value with `--key`. `--app` disambiguates a stanza that exists in more than one app.

#### Set keys on a stanza

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile and the named file and stanza. Impact: the listed keys are written; the stanza is created if it does not exist. Preview with `splunkctl conf set macros my_macro definition='index=main sourcetype=syslog'`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl conf get macros my_macro`.

```bash
splunkctl conf set macros my_macro definition='index=main sourcetype=syslog'
splunkctl conf set macros my_macro definition='index=main sourcetype=syslog' --yes
splunkctl conf get macros my_macro
```

Expected result: the preview names the file and stanza and shows a field-level diff, old value on the left, new value on the right, `add` for a brand-new key:

```text
[DRY RUN] Set 1 key(s) on 'my_macro' in macros.conf (profile: uat @ uat.splunk.internal:8089)
  file: macros.conf
  stanza: my_macro
  definition: index=old -> index=main sourcetype=syslog
Pass --yes to apply.
```

`conf set` creates the stanza when it is missing; there is no separate create step.

#### Clear a key

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile and the named file and stanza. Impact: the key is set to the empty string; the REST API cannot delete a key. Preview with `splunkctl conf unset macros my_macro definition`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl conf get macros my_macro --key definition`.

```bash
splunkctl conf unset macros my_macro definition
splunkctl conf unset macros my_macro definition --yes
```

Expected result: the key reads back empty. This is the same mechanism `parsers unset` uses. To remove a whole stanza, use the dedicated command group for that file when one exists (for example `parsers delete` for `props.conf`).

#### Reload the file

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: splunkd re-reads the named conf file so the change takes effect without a restart. Preview with `splunkctl conf reload macros`, apply with `splunkctl conf reload macros --yes`, and verify with `splunkctl conf get macros my_macro`.

```bash
splunkctl conf reload macros --yes
```

Reload after a `set` or `unset` when the change must take effect immediately.

### Troubleshooting

- `not_found` from `get`: the stanza lives in another app; rerun with `--app APP`, or list with `splunkctl conf list FILE --app APP`.
- `not_found` from `set` on a file: the conf file name is wrong; check `splunkctl conf files --filter <text>` and drop the `.conf` suffix.
- `permission` from `set`, `unset`, or `reload`: the account cannot write that file; `authorize.conf` and `server.conf` need `admin_all_objects`.
- A key still shows the old value after `set --yes`: run `splunkctl conf reload FILE --yes`, or the value is overridden by a higher-precedence app or a `default` layer.
- `unset` leaves the key present: expected, REST sets it to an empty string; remove the stanza through its dedicated group instead.

### See also

- [Manage macros, eventtypes, tags](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/knowledge.md)
- [Manage source types and extractions](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/parsers.md)
- [Manage configuration as code](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/state.md)
- [Command reference: conf](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/conf.md)

## Set up the MCP server

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/mcp.md


When to use: you want an AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, or any other [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) client) to query and change your Splunk Enterprise and Splunk SOAR instances through splunkctl, with the same dry-run guard the CLI applies.

### Prerequisites

- splunkctl installed (`pip install splunkctl`, see [Install](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/install.md)).
- A working profile: `splunkctl doctor` passes for Splunk and, if you use SOAR, `splunkctl soar test` passes (see [Configure](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/configure.md) and [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)).
- A least-privilege Splunk account. The server inherits whatever your credentials can do.
- An MCP client that can launch a stdio command or connect to a local HTTP URL.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl mcp serve [--transport stdio|http] [--host 127.0.0.1|localhost|::1] [--port N]
splunkctl mcp install [--transport stdio|http] [--host 127.0.0.1|localhost|::1] [--port N]
```

`serve` starts the server (stdio by default). `install` writes a `splunkctl` entry into `.mcp.json` in the current directory for Claude Code. `--host` and `--port` apply only to `--transport http`; the default listener is `127.0.0.1:8765` and the MCP URL is `http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp`.

### Workflow

#### Install splunkctl

```bash
pip install splunkctl
```

Or install from source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/dannyota/splunkctl.git
cd splunkctl && pip install -e .
```

Expected result: `splunkctl --version` prints the version.

#### Configure credentials

The MCP server reads the same config as the CLI. Either export environment variables:

```bash
export SPLUNK_HOST=your-splunk-host
export SPLUNK_PORT=8089
export SPLUNK_USER=admin
export SPLUNK_PASS=your-password
```

or write `~/.splunkctl/config.yaml` with `splunkctl config init`, and add SOAR credentials with `splunkctl config init --soar`. Then verify:

```bash
splunkctl doctor
splunkctl soar test
```

Expected result: both commands exit 0. Credentials stay in the config file (mode 0600) or the environment, never in the MCP client config, unless you choose to put them there as in the Claude Desktop example below.

#### Register with Claude Code

```bash
splunkctl mcp install
```

Expected result: `.mcp.json` in the current directory gains a `splunkctl` server entry that runs the current Python interpreter with `-m splunkctl mcp serve`. An existing `.mcp.json` is merged, not replaced. Restart Claude Code to pick up the server.

#### Register with Claude Desktop

Add this to `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "splunkctl": {
      "command": "splunkctl",
      "args": ["mcp", "serve"],
      "env": {
        "SPLUNK_HOST": "your-splunk-host",
        "SPLUNK_PORT": "8089",
        "SPLUNK_USER": "admin",
        "SPLUNK_PASS": "your-password"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Expected result: after a restart, Claude Desktop lists the `splunkctl` tools. Omit `env` if `~/.splunkctl/config.yaml` exists.

#### Point Cursor or another client at stdio

```bash
splunkctl mcp serve
```

Expected result: the server speaks MCP over stdin and stdout, one agent per process, with no network listener. Pass `SPLUNK_HOST`, `SPLUNK_PORT`, `SPLUNK_USER`, and `SPLUNK_PASS` as environment variables, or make sure `~/.splunkctl/config.yaml` exists.

#### Run the Streamable HTTP transport

For local clients that need a URL instead of a command:

```bash
splunkctl mcp serve --transport http
splunkctl mcp serve --transport http --host localhost --port 9000
splunkctl mcp install --transport http
splunkctl mcp install --transport http --host ::1 --port 9000
```

Expected result: a Streamable HTTP listener on `127.0.0.1:8765` (or the host and port you pass) serving `/mcp`, and `install --transport http` writes a URL-based entry instead of a command entry. The host is restricted to `127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, or `::1`; a non-loopback address is a usage error. HTTP mode has no authentication of its own, so anything on the machine that can reach the port can call the tools with your credentials.

#### Discover tools progressively

The server uses dynamic tool loading. It starts with five meta-tools and loads typed, group-specific tools on demand, which keeps the agent's context window small while still covering every command. It is built on MCP Python SDK 2 (`mcp>=2.3`) and sends `tools/list_changed` notifications whenever `focus`, `unfocus`, or `usage` changes the tool list.

- Meta-tools, always loaded: `help`, `usage`, `focus`, `unfocus`, `run`.
- Group tools, loaded by `focus` (for example `focus group="rules"` loads `rules_list`, `rules_get`, and so on).
- Resources, one per guide, at `guide://{name}`.
- Prompts: `investigate-ioc`, `triage-notable`, `audit-detection`, and `export-state`.

A typical sequence:

```text
help                          list command groups
help group="rules"            list subcommands in a group
focus group="rules"           load typed tools with full parameter schemas
rules_list ...                call the typed tools
unfocus group="rules"         free the context when done
run command="search oneshot 'index=main | stats count' --earliest -1h"
```

`usage command="soar playbooks run"` shows one command's flags and loads it as a callable tool without focusing the whole group. `run` is an escape hatch for raw command strings with no argument validation. The `soar` tree has nested subgroups, so focus at subgroup granularity: `focus group="soar containers"`, not `focus group="soar"`. All tool output is JSON.

Example exchanges:

> **You:** How many failed login events are there in the last hour?
>
> The agent calls `run command="search oneshot 'index=main sourcetype=linux_secure action=failure | stats count' --earliest -1h"` and returns the count.

> **You:** Show me the detection rules that fire most often.
>
> The agent calls `focus group="rules"`, then `rules_list`, then `focus group="alerts"` and `alerts_list` to see which fired recently.

> **You:** List open SOAR containers from the last 24 hours.
>
> The agent calls `focus group="soar containers"`, then `soar_containers_list` with the matching filters.

#### Apply a guarded change

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk or SOAR host in the profile the server was started with. Impact: the same change the CLI command makes. Preview by calling the tool without `yes`, apply by calling it again with `yes=true`, and verify with the matching read tool (for example `rules_get` after `rules_update`).

Guarded tools carry `[guarded: dry-run by default, pass yes=true to apply]` in their description and a `yes` parameter. Without `yes=true` the call returns the dry-run preview and changes nothing, exactly like the CLI without `--yes`:

```text
rules_disable name="Old brute force rule"            preview only
rules_disable name="Old brute force rule" yes=true   apply
```

The same holds for `run`: include `--yes` in the command string to apply.

```bash
splunkctl rules get "Old brute force rule"
```

Expected result: the read-back shows `disabled: 1` after the apply.

### Troubleshooting

- `config` error or "No Splunk host configured" from every tool: the server process cannot see your profile. Export `SPLUNK_HOST` and friends in the client's `env`, or create `~/.splunkctl/config.yaml` with `splunkctl config init`.
- `auth` error: the credentials in the server's environment are wrong or expired. Run `splunkctl doctor` in the same environment the client uses.
- `connection` or `timeout` error: the server cannot reach the Splunk management port. Check `SPLUNK_HOST` and `SPLUNK_PORT` (8089 by default) and any VPN.
- `confirmation_required` error from `run`: the SPL contains a write command (`outputlookup`, `collect`, and others). Add `--yes` to the command string only if the write is intended.
- A guarded tool "did nothing": the call ran as a dry run. Pass `yes=true`.
- `--host 0.0.0.0` is rejected: HTTP mode binds only to a loopback address by design. Put a reverse proxy with authentication in front if you need remote access.
- The client does not list the server after `mcp install`: restart the client, and check that `.mcp.json` sits in the directory the client opened.

### See also

- [Install](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/install.md)
- [Configure](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/configure.md)
- [Diagnose a connection](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/doctor.md)
- [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)
- [Run searches](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/search.md)
- [Command reference: mcp](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/mcp.md)

## Log in through browser SAML

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/auth.md


When to use: your Splunk or SOAR instance authenticates through a SAML identity provider (with or without a second factor), so a username and password or a token cannot be stored in the profile, and you want every splunkctl command to reuse one browser login until it expires.

### Prerequisites

- splunkctl with the browser extra and Chromium:

  ```bash
  python -m pip install 'splunkctl[browser]'
  python -m playwright install chromium
  ```

  Configuration succeeds without them; `splunkctl auth login` prints these commands when they are missing.

- A machine with a display: login opens a headed Chromium window. The browser handles the identity provider; splunkctl never reads or stores TOTP secrets or codes.
- A profile in browser mode (`auth_mode: browser` with a `web_url`), written by `config init` as shown below.
- Not supported: reading or storing TOTP secrets, native Splunk Duo or RSA flows, OpenID Connect or OAuth, logging in to both products in one command, and a local splunkctl callback redirect.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl config init --web-url <https://splunk.example.com:8000> [--profile NAME] [--auth-mode auto|browser]
splunkctl config init --soar --web-url <https://soar.example.com> [--sso-url URL] [--profile NAME]
splunkctl auth login --target <siem|soar>
splunkctl auth status [--target siem|soar|both]
splunkctl auth logout [--target siem|soar|both]
```

### Workflow

#### Detect SAML during setup

```bash
splunkctl config init --web-url https://splunk.example.com:8000
splunkctl config init --soar --web-url https://soar.example.com --sso-url 'https://soar.example.com/saml2/login?idp=okta&next=/'
```

Expected result: `config init` probes the product's public login route. When it sees a redirect to an external identity provider it records `auth_mode: browser` and stores the product `web_url` in the profile. SAML detection runs only when `--web-url` is given. Pass `--auth-mode browser` to force browser mode without probing. For SOAR, pass `--sso-url` because SOAR's `/login` route is local-only.

#### Log in

```bash
splunkctl auth login --target siem
splunkctl auth login --target soar
```

Expected result: Chromium opens at the product login route; you complete the identity provider prompts, including any TOTP code; splunkctl extracts only the product session (the Splunk `splunkd_<port>` cookie, or the SOAR `sessionid` and `csrftoken` cookies), proves it against the product API, and prints `siem session stored (profile 'NAME').`. `login` requires exactly one target because two back-to-back browser flows are easy to confuse.

#### Check the session

```bash
splunkctl auth status
splunkctl auth status --target siem
```

Expected result: one row per target with `status` set to `missing`, `valid`, `expired`, or `unreachable`. Without `--target`, only targets configured for browser mode are checked; if none are, it prints `No browser-authenticated targets configured.`.

#### Use the session from normal commands

```bash
splunkctl search oneshot 'index=_internal | head 5'
splunkctl soar test
```

Expected result: commands reuse the cached session whenever the active profile selects browser mode. A missing or expired session never opens a browser; the command fails with the exact `splunkctl auth login --target ...` instruction to run instead.

#### Log out

```bash
splunkctl auth logout --target siem
splunkctl auth logout --target both
```

Expected result: a best-effort remote logout, then `Logout complete.`. The local session is always removed, even if the remote endpoint refuses; a refused remote logout prints a warning.

Sessions live under `~/.splunkctl/sessions/<profile>/<target>.json` with directory mode `0700` and file mode `0600`. A record holds only the target, profile, product origin, product session values, and validation timestamps. It never stores passwords, Playwright storage state, identity-provider cookies, or TOTP secrets, and session values are redacted from all output.

### Troubleshooting

- `usage` error `siem is configured for token authentication, not browser login`: the profile has `auth_mode: token` or `password`; rerun `splunkctl config init --web-url URL` so SAML is detected, or pass `--auth-mode browser`.
- `login` prints `pip install` and `playwright install` commands: the browser extra is missing; run them and retry.
- `auth` error `login finished but the product session was rejected`: the browser ended on a different origin than `web_url`, or the identity provider flow did not complete; check `web_url` with `splunkctl config show` and log in again.
- `connection` error `SIEM is unreachable while checking the browser session`: the product API is down or blocked; fix connectivity with [Diagnose a connection](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/doctor.md).
- A command reports the session is missing or expired: run the `splunkctl auth login --target ...` command it prints; commands never open a browser on their own.
- `remote logout failed; clearing local session`: the product refused the logout call; the local file is still removed and a new `login` is required.

### See also

- [Configure](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/configure.md)
- [Install](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/install.md)
- [Set up and check SOAR](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar.md)
- [Contributor lab: Keycloak SAML](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/keycloak-lab.md)
- [Command reference: auth](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/auth.md)

## Diagnose a connection

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/doctor.md


When to use: you have just configured a profile, a command fails and you need to know whether the problem is the config file, the network, credentials, the license, or permissions, or a CI job or agent must confirm the instance is usable before it starts.

### Prerequisites

- splunkctl installed and a profile written with `splunkctl config init` (see [Configure](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/configure.md)). Without a config file, `doctor` warns and falls back to defaults and environment variables.
- Network access to the Splunk REST port (8089 by default). The Web UI check is optional and only matters for lookup upload and app install.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl doctor [--strict] [--json]
splunkctl config test
splunkctl info
```

### Workflow

#### Run after setup

```bash
splunkctl doctor
```

Expected result: a check list on standard error, grouped as Config, Connection, Auth, Server, Health, KV Store, Permissions, Web UI, SOAR, and MCP, followed by `N/M passed, W warnings, F failures`. The checks are:

1. Config: the config file in use, including the `profiles.yaml` fallback when Splunk's own CLI owns `config.yaml`.
2. Connection: the REST API is reachable.
3. Auth: the credentials are valid, with the user name.
4. Server: Splunk version, OS, mode, and license state.
5. Health: `splunkd` health (green) and system messages with severity `error`.
6. KV store: status is `ready`.
7. Permissions: roles, then nine key capabilities: `search`, `admin_all_objects`, `edit_user`, `edit_roles`, `edit_tcp`, `edit_monitor`, `list_inputs`, `rest_apps_management`, `change_own_password`.
8. Web UI: the Splunk Web login page answers (needed for lookup upload and app install).
9. SOAR: connection, auth, health, and license, or `SKIP` when the profile has no `soar:` section.
10. MCP: a `splunkctl` entry exists in `.mcp.json` in the current directory.

Each failed check prints a `hint:` line naming the fix. Exit code is `0` when no check has status `FAIL` and `1` otherwise; warnings (`WARN`) do not fail the run unless you pass `--strict`.

#### Gate a CI pipeline

```bash
splunkctl doctor --strict
```

Expected result: exit 1 on any failure or warning, so the pipeline stops early when the instance is unreachable, the license is not `OK`, the KV store is down, or the service account lacks a capability.

#### Bootstrap an agent

```bash
splunkctl doctor --json | jq '.[] | select(.status == "FAIL")'
```

Expected result: the human-readable list still goes to standard error, and a JSON array of `{check, status, detail, hint}` objects goes to standard output. `status` is `OK`, `WARN`, `FAIL`, or `SKIP`. An agent should call `doctor --json` at session start, parse the array, and abort with a clear message when any check is `FAIL`.

#### Isolate a failure layer

```bash
splunkctl doctor
splunkctl config test
splunkctl info
```

Expected result: `doctor` stops at the first layer that fails (config, then connection), so the first `FAIL` tells you whether to fix the file, the network, the credentials, the license, or a role. `config test` repeats only the connect-and-login step with a classified error (`auth`, `connection`, `timeout`); `info` prints the server details once authentication works.

### Troubleshooting

- `Config` fails with `Splunk-format config`: `~/.splunkctl/config.yaml` belongs to Splunk's CLI; run `splunkctl config init --path ~/.splunkctl/profiles.yaml` or see [Relationship to Splunk's splunkctl](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/splunk-cli.md).
- `Config` warns `not found`: run `splunkctl config init`, or set `SPLUNK_HOST` and `SPLUNK_TOKEN`.
- `REST API reachable` fails (`connection` or `timeout`): check `SPLUNK_HOST` and `SPLUNK_PORT`, that splunkd is running, and that port 8089 is open from this machine (`curl -k https://HOST:8089/services/server/info`).
- `Authenticated` fails, or `REST API reachable` fails with a login error (`auth`): verify `SPLUNK_USER` and `SPLUNK_PASS` or `SPLUNK_TOKEN`, or the profile's values with `splunkctl config show`.
- `License` warns: run `splunkctl server license`; a trial or expired license is reported in the detail.
- `Splunkd health` or `System messages` warns: run `splunkctl server messages`; dismiss a stale message with `splunkctl server messages --dismiss NAME --yes`.
- `KV Store` warns `failed`: ask the Splunk admin to restart Splunk or check `mongod.log`; `kvstore` commands return `http` 503 until it is `ready`.
- `cap:<name>` fails (`permission` later on): grant that capability to your user or role.
- `Web UI reachable` warns: lookup upload and app install need Splunk Web; other commands work.
- `MCP registered` warns: run `splunkctl mcp install` from the project directory, or ignore it when you are not using the MCP server.

### See also

- [Configure](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/configure.md)
- [Install](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/install.md)
- [Check server health and topology](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/server.md)
- [Set up the MCP server](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/mcp.md)
- [Exit codes](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/exit-codes.md)

## Manage indexes

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/indexes.md


When to use: you are onboarding a new data source that needs its own retention or access boundary, resizing an index that is approaching its limit, checking retention against a compliance requirement, or decommissioning an index.

### Prerequisites

- A profile that passes `splunkctl doctor` (see [Configure](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/configure.md)).
- An account allowed to manage indexes (`indexes_edit`, which the `admin` role has).
- A retention plan: `--frozen-period` is in seconds (86400 = 1 day, 2592000 = 30 days, 31536000 = 365 days) and `--max-size` is in MB.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl indexes list [--filter SUBSTRING] [--limit N] [--offset N]
splunkctl indexes get <NAME>
splunkctl indexes create --name <NAME> [--datatype event|metric] [--max-size MB] [--frozen-period SECONDS] [--home-path PATH] [--cold-path PATH] [--yes]
splunkctl indexes update <NAME> [--max-size MB] [--frozen-period SECONDS] [--yes]
splunkctl indexes clean <NAME> [--clean-timeout SECONDS] [--yes]
splunkctl indexes delete <NAME> [--yes]
splunkctl indexes reload [--yes]
```

### Workflow

#### List and check capacity

```bash
splunkctl indexes list
splunkctl indexes get main
splunkctl indexes list --json | jq '.[] | {name, totalEventCount, currentDBSizeMB, maxTotalDataSizeMB}'
```

Expected result: one row per index with size and event counts; `get` prints every setting. Field values arrive as strings, so convert before arithmetic in `jq`:

```bash
splunkctl indexes list --json \
  | jq '.[] | select((.currentDBSizeMB | tonumber) / (.maxTotalDataSizeMB | tonumber) > 0.8)
        | {name, pct_used: (100 * (.currentDBSizeMB | tonumber) / (.maxTotalDataSizeMB | tonumber))}'
splunkctl indexes list --json | jq '[.[] | select(.totalEventCount == "0")] | .[].name'
splunkctl indexes get security_logs --json | jq '{frozenTimePeriodInSecs, maxTotalDataSizeMB}'
```

The first query lists indexes over 80 percent full, the second indexes with zero events (possibly misconfigured inputs), and the third verifies retention settings against a compliance requirement.

#### Create indexes for security workloads

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: a new index is created and starts accepting events from any input that names it. Preview with `splunkctl indexes create --name threat_intel --max-size 100 --frozen-period 7776000`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl indexes get threat_intel`.

```bash
splunkctl indexes create --name threat_intel --max-size 100 --frozen-period 7776000
splunkctl indexes create --name threat_intel --max-size 100 --frozen-period 7776000 --yes
splunkctl indexes create --name security_logs --max-size 5000 --frozen-period 31536000 --yes
splunkctl indexes create --name metrics_idx --datatype metric --max-size 500 --frozen-period 604800 --yes
```

Expected result: the index appears in `splunkctl indexes list`. The first example keeps threat intel for 90 days in a small index; the second keeps security logs for 365 days in a large one; the third creates a metrics index. Separate indexes let you apply different retention per data tier and control access through roles. `--home-path` and `--cold-path` set bucket locations on the server when the defaults do not fit.

#### Change size or retention

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: lowering `--max-size` or `--frozen-period` makes Splunk freeze (and by default delete) buckets sooner. Preview with `splunkctl indexes update my_index --frozen-period 2592000`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl indexes get my_index --json | jq '{frozenTimePeriodInSecs, maxTotalDataSizeMB}'`.

```bash
splunkctl indexes update my_index --max-size 1000
splunkctl indexes update my_index --max-size 1000 --yes
splunkctl indexes update my_index --frozen-period 2592000 --yes
```

Expected result: the new values read back from `get`. `maxTotalDataSizeMB` is a high-water mark; Splunk freezes buckets when the index reaches it, so plan for headroom. At least one of `--max-size` or `--frozen-period` is required.

#### Remove all events from an index

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: every event in the index is deleted; the index itself and its settings remain. Preview with `splunkctl indexes clean my_index`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl indexes get my_index --json | jq .totalEventCount`.

```bash
splunkctl indexes clean my_index
splunkctl indexes clean my_index --yes
splunkctl indexes clean big_index --clean-timeout 300 --yes
```

Expected result: `Index 'my_index' cleaned.`. The CLI waits up to `--clean-timeout` seconds (default 60) for the index to empty; a large index needs a longer wait.

#### Delete an index

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: the index and its searchable data are removed from Splunk; inputs that still name it will drop events to the last-chance index or fail. Preview with `splunkctl indexes delete my_index`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl indexes list --filter my_index`.

```bash
splunkctl indexes delete my_index
splunkctl indexes delete my_index --yes
```

Expected result: the index no longer lists. Deleting an index does not free disk immediately; frozen buckets remain on the filesystem until removed on the Splunk server.

#### Reload index configuration

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: splunkd re-reads every index configuration. Preview with `splunkctl indexes reload`, apply with `splunkctl indexes reload --yes`, and verify with `splunkctl indexes list`.

```bash
splunkctl indexes reload --yes
```

### Troubleshooting

- `not_found` from `get`, `update`, `clean`, or `delete`: index names are case-sensitive; check `splunkctl indexes list --filter <text>`.
- `No settings to update`: `update` needs `--max-size` or `--frozen-period`.
- `Clean did not finish ... Retry with a larger --clean-timeout`: the index did not empty in time; the message reports whether the index is enabled and how many events remain. Rerun with `--clean-timeout 300` or more.
- `conflict` from `create`: an index with that name already exists; use `update` instead.
- `permission` from `create`, `update`, `clean`, or `delete`: the account lacks `indexes_edit`; use an `admin` account.
- `jq` errors such as `number and string cannot be divided`: wrap fields in `tonumber` as shown above.

### See also

- [Manage data inputs](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/inputs.md)
- [Manage HEC tokens](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/hec.md)
- [Manage users and roles](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/users.md), for index access per role
- [Command reference: indexes](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/indexes.md)

## Manage data inputs

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/inputs.md


When to use: you are onboarding a new log source, routing it to a dedicated index and sourcetype, pausing an input for maintenance, or removing a decommissioned source, all over the REST API without filesystem access to the Splunk server.

### Prerequisites

- A profile that passes `splunkctl doctor` with the `list_inputs`, `edit_monitor` (file inputs), and `edit_tcp` (network inputs) capabilities it reports.
- The target index already exists (see [Manage indexes](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/indexes.md)); events for a missing index are dropped or sent to the last-chance index.
- For `tcp` and `udp` inputs: the port is free on the Splunk server.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl inputs list [--kind monitor|tcp|udp|script|http] [--filter SUBSTRING] [--limit N] [--offset N]
splunkctl inputs get <NAME>
splunkctl inputs create --name <NAME> --kind <monitor|tcp|udp|script|http> [--index INDEX] [--sourcetype SOURCETYPE] [--disabled] [--yes]
splunkctl inputs update <NAME> [--index INDEX] [--sourcetype SOURCETYPE] [--enabled|--disabled] [--yes]
splunkctl inputs enable <NAME> [--yes]
splunkctl inputs disable <NAME> [--yes]
splunkctl inputs delete <NAME> [--yes]
```

`NAME` is the input's path for `monitor` and `script` inputs (`/var/log/syslog`) and the port for `tcp` and `udp` inputs (`5514`). `http` inputs are HEC tokens; manage them with [Manage HEC tokens](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/hec.md).

### Workflow

#### Audit existing inputs

```bash
splunkctl inputs list
splunkctl inputs list --kind monitor
splunkctl inputs get /var/log/syslog
splunkctl inputs list --kind monitor --json | jq '.[] | {name, index, sourcetype, disabled}'
```

Expected result: one row per input with `name`, `kind`, `index`, `sourcetype`, and `disabled`. `--filter`, `--limit`, and `--offset` apply client side after `--kind`. The SDK's union collection pages each kind with a 30-per-kind default limit, so an instance with more than 30 inputs of one kind may list incompletely; verify completeness for a kind with:

```bash
splunkctl search oneshot '| rest /services/data/inputs/monitor' --limit 10000
```

#### Onboard a new log source

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: Splunk starts reading the file or listening on the port and indexing into the named index immediately. Preview with `splunkctl inputs create --name /var/log/webapp/access.log --kind monitor --index security_logs --sourcetype access_combined`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl inputs get /var/log/webapp/access.log`.

```bash
splunkctl inputs create --name /var/log/webapp/access.log --kind monitor --index security_logs --sourcetype access_combined
splunkctl inputs create --name /var/log/webapp/access.log --kind monitor --index security_logs --sourcetype access_combined --yes
splunkctl inputs create --name 5514 --kind tcp --index security_logs --sourcetype syslog --yes
splunkctl inputs create --name /var/log/staged.log --kind monitor --index main --disabled --yes
```

Expected result: `Created input: NAME (KIND)`. The preview lists `kind`, `index`, and `sourcetype`. `--disabled` creates the input paused so you can review it before data flows. TCP and UDP inputs bind a port on the Splunk server, so confirm it is not already in use.

#### Verify data is arriving

```bash
splunkctl search run 'index=security_logs sourcetype=access_combined | head 5' --earliest -15m
```

Expected result: recent events from the new input. An empty result after several minutes usually means a wrong path or port, a missing index, or a disabled input.

#### Change index or sourcetype

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: new events from the input are parsed and stored differently from now on; existing events are unchanged. Preview with `splunkctl inputs update /var/log/app.log --sourcetype json`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl inputs get /var/log/app.log`.

```bash
splunkctl inputs update /var/log/app.log --sourcetype json
splunkctl inputs update /var/log/app.log --sourcetype json --yes
splunkctl inputs update /var/log/app.log --index security_logs --enabled --yes
```

#### Pause an input for maintenance

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: ingestion stops while the input is disabled; the configuration is kept, and file inputs resume from where they left off when re-enabled. Preview with `splunkctl inputs disable /var/log/old_app.log`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl inputs get /var/log/old_app.log --json` (check `disabled`).

```bash
splunkctl inputs disable /var/log/old_app.log --yes
splunkctl inputs enable /var/log/old_app.log --yes
```

Use disable for maintenance windows instead of deleting the input.

#### Remove a decommissioned source

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: the input definition is removed; indexed events remain searchable. Preview with `splunkctl inputs delete /var/log/retired_app.log`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl inputs list --filter retired_app`.

```bash
splunkctl inputs delete /var/log/retired_app.log
splunkctl inputs delete /var/log/retired_app.log --yes
```

### Troubleshooting

- `Input not found: NAME`: the name must match exactly (full path for files, bare port for TCP and UDP); find it with `splunkctl inputs list --filter <text>`, and remember the 30-per-kind listing limit.
- `conflict` or a create error naming an existing input: the path or port is already configured; `update` it instead.
- `permission` from `create`, `update`, or `delete`: the account lacks `edit_monitor` or `edit_tcp`; check `splunkctl doctor`.
- No events after `create --yes`: the input was created `--disabled`, the index does not exist, or the file path is not readable by the Splunk process on the server.
- `--kind http` behaves differently: those are HEC tokens; use `splunkctl hec` for the full token lifecycle.

### See also

- [Manage indexes](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/indexes.md)
- [Manage HEC tokens](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/hec.md)
- [Manage source types and extractions](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/parsers.md)
- [Run searches](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/search.md)
- [Command reference: inputs](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/inputs.md)

## Manage HEC tokens

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/hec.md


When to use: a SOAR playbook, custom script, CI pipeline, or cloud webhook needs to push events into Splunk without a forwarder, and you must provision, rotate, or revoke the HTTP Event Collector (HEC) token it uses, or confirm that HEC is enabled and accepting events.

### Prerequisites

- A profile that passes `splunkctl doctor` and an account allowed to manage HTTP inputs (the `admin` role covers it).
- For `send`: network access from this machine to the HEC port (8088 by default), which is separate from the 8089 management port.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl hec list [--filter SUBSTRING] [--limit N] [--offset N]
splunkctl hec get <NAME>
splunkctl hec create --name <NAME> [--index INDEX] [--indexes A,B] [--sourcetype SOURCETYPE] [--set KEY=VALUE]... [--yes]
splunkctl hec enable <NAME> [--yes]
splunkctl hec disable <NAME> [--yes]
splunkctl hec delete <NAME> [--yes]
splunkctl hec settings [--enable|--disable] [--yes]
splunkctl hec send <NAME> <EVENT> [--index INDEX] [--sourcetype SOURCETYPE] [--yes]
```

Splunk stores HEC token names with an `http://` prefix internally, so creating `my_token` produces a token named `http://my_token`. The CLI handles this for you; always use the short name.

### Workflow

#### Audit existing tokens

```bash
splunkctl hec list
splunkctl hec get soar_enrichment
splunkctl hec list --json | jq '.[] | {name, index, disabled}'
```

Expected result: one row per token with `name`, `token`, `index`, `disabled`, and `sourcetype`; `get` adds `indexes` (the allowlist) and `useACK`. Both print the token value, so treat their output as a secret.

#### Check or toggle HEC globally

```bash
splunkctl hec settings
```

Expected result: `disabled`, `port`, `enableSSL`, and `dedicatedIoThreads` for the HEC input as a whole. Tokens only work when HEC is enabled globally.

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: every HEC token on the instance starts or stops accepting events. Preview with `splunkctl hec settings --enable`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl hec settings` (check `disabled`).

```bash
splunkctl hec settings --enable --yes
splunkctl hec settings --disable --yes
```

#### Provision a token for an integration

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: a new ingestion credential is created and can write to the named indexes immediately. Preview with `splunkctl hec create --name soar_enrichment --index notable_enrichments --sourcetype json`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl hec get soar_enrichment`.

```bash
splunkctl hec create --name soar_enrichment --index notable_enrichments --sourcetype json
splunkctl hec create --name soar_enrichment --index notable_enrichments --sourcetype json --yes
splunkctl hec create --name threat_feed_ingest --index threat_intel --indexes threat_intel --sourcetype stix_ioc --yes
splunkctl hec create --name deploy_events --index main --set useACK=1 --yes
```

Expected result: `HEC token 'NAME' created.`. `--index` is the default index, `--indexes` the comma-separated allowlist a sender may target, and `--set KEY=VALUE` passes any other token property (for example `useACK=1`).

#### Rotate a compromised token

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: senders using the old token are rejected as soon as it is disabled. Preview with `splunkctl hec disable old_webhook_token`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl hec get old_webhook_token --json` (check `disabled`).

```bash
splunkctl hec disable old_webhook_token --yes
splunkctl hec create --name new_webhook_token --index webhook_events --sourcetype json --yes
splunkctl hec get new_webhook_token --json
```

Expected result: the old token shows `disabled: 1`; copy the new token value from `get` into the sender, then delete the old token once nothing uses it. `enable` reverses a disable.

#### Send a test event

> **Safety:** Target is the HEC endpoint of the Splunk host in the active profile, on the port from `hec settings`. Impact: one event is indexed into the token's default index or `--index`. Preview with `splunkctl hec send soar_enrichment '{"test": true}'`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl search oneshot 'index=notable_enrichments test=true' --earliest -15m`.

```bash
splunkctl hec send soar_enrichment '{"test": true}'
splunkctl hec send soar_enrichment '{"test": true}' --index notable_enrichments --sourcetype json --yes
```

Expected result: `Event sent.`. The CLI reads the token value and the global HEC port and TLS setting, then POSTs to `/services/collector/event` with `Authorization: Splunk <token>`, honouring the profile's `verify` setting.

#### Revoke a decommissioned integration

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: the token is deleted and cannot be recovered; any sender still using it is rejected. Preview with `splunkctl hec delete legacy_siem_bridge`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl hec list --filter legacy_siem_bridge`.

```bash
splunkctl hec delete legacy_siem_bridge
splunkctl hec delete legacy_siem_bridge --yes
```

### Troubleshooting

- `not_found` from `get`, `enable`, `disable`, `delete`, or `send`: use the short name without the `http://` prefix and check `splunkctl hec list`.
- `Create failed` naming an existing token: the name is taken; pick another or delete the old one.
- `HEC send failed` with a server message such as `Invalid token` or `Incorrect index`: the token is disabled, HEC is globally disabled, or `--index` is not in the token's allowed indexes.
- `connection` or `timeout` from `send` only: the HEC port (8088) is blocked while the management port is open; open it or send from a host that can reach it.
- `permission` from `create` or `delete`: the account cannot manage HTTP inputs; use an `admin` account.

### See also

- [Manage data inputs](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/inputs.md)
- [Manage indexes](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/indexes.md)
- [Run searches](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/search.md)
- [Install](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/install.md)
- [Command reference: hec](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/hec.md)

## Manage apps

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/apps.md


When to use: you need to deploy or upgrade a Technology Add-on, a content pack such as Enterprise Security content, or a custom detection app on a remote instance, disable an app during an incident, or audit what is installed, without SSH or the Web UI.

### Prerequisites

- A profile that passes `splunkctl doctor`, including the `Web UI reachable` check: `install` uploads the package through the Splunk Web UI handler.
- An account allowed to install and edit apps (for example the `admin` role).
- For `install`: a local `.spl` or `.tar.gz` package.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl apps list [--filter SUBSTRING] [--limit N] [--offset N]
splunkctl apps get <NAME>
splunkctl apps install --path <PACKAGE.spl|PACKAGE.tar.gz> [--force] [--yes]
splunkctl apps update <NAME> [--enabled|--disabled] [--visible|--hidden] [--yes]
splunkctl apps uninstall <NAME> [--yes]
splunkctl apps reload [--yes]
```

### Workflow

#### List and inspect

```bash
splunkctl apps list
splunkctl apps list --filter TA-
splunkctl apps get SplunkForwarder
splunkctl apps list --json | jq '.[] | {name, version, disabled}'
```

Expected result: one row per installed app; `get` prints the app's full settings. `--filter`, `--limit`, and `--offset` apply client side.

#### Install or upgrade from a local package

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: the package is uploaded through Splunk Web and installed; with `--force` an existing app of the same name is overwritten. Preview with `splunkctl apps install --path ./Splunk_TA_windows-8.9.0.spl`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl apps get Splunk_TA_windows`.

```bash
splunkctl apps install --path ./Splunk_TA_windows-8.9.0.spl
splunkctl apps install --path ./Splunk_TA_windows-8.9.0.spl --yes
splunkctl apps install --path ./DA-ESS-ContentUpdate-4.29.0.spl --force --yes
```

Expected result: the app appears in `splunkctl apps list`. The upload goes from your machine to the Splunk Web UI handler, so no SSH, SCP, or server filesystem access is needed. `--force` is required when the app already exists on the instance (reinstall or upgrade). An install may still need a Splunk restart to activate new modular inputs or scripted lookups; the CLI does not restart Splunk.

#### Disable an app during an incident

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: the app's scheduled searches and knowledge objects stop running until re-enabled. Preview with `splunkctl apps update SplunkEnterpriseSecuritySuite --disabled`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl apps get SplunkEnterpriseSecuritySuite --json` (check `disabled`).

```bash
splunkctl apps update SplunkEnterpriseSecuritySuite --disabled
splunkctl apps update SplunkEnterpriseSecuritySuite --disabled --yes
splunkctl apps update SplunkEnterpriseSecuritySuite --enabled --yes
splunkctl apps update my_app --enabled --visible --yes
splunkctl apps update my_app --disabled --hidden --yes
```

Expected result: `Updated app 'NAME'.`. `--visible` and `--hidden` control whether the app shows in the Splunk Web app menu; at least one of the four flags is required.

#### Uninstall an app

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: the app and its configuration are removed from the instance. Preview with `splunkctl apps uninstall my_app`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl apps list --filter my_app`.

```bash
splunkctl apps uninstall my_app
splunkctl apps uninstall my_app --yes
```

#### Reload all apps after a bulk change

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: every app's configuration is re-read by splunkd. Preview with `splunkctl apps reload`, apply with `splunkctl apps reload --yes`, and verify with `splunkctl apps list`.

```bash
splunkctl apps reload --yes
```

### Troubleshooting

- `not_found` from `get`, `update`, or `uninstall`: the app id (directory name) differs from its label; find it with `splunkctl apps list --filter <text>`.
- `App install failed` or a `web` error: Splunk Web is not reachable from this machine; run `splunkctl doctor` and check `Web UI reachable`.
- Install fails because the app already exists: add `--force`.
- `No settings specified`: `update` needs `--enabled`, `--disabled`, `--visible`, or `--hidden`.
- `permission` on `update` or `uninstall`: the account lacks app administration rights; use an `admin` account.
- New inputs or lookups from an installed app do not run: restart Splunk from the server; the CLI does not restart it.

### See also

- [Diagnose a connection](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/doctor.md)
- [Manage detection rules](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/rules.md)
- [Manage configuration as code](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/state.md)
- [Command reference: apps](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/apps.md)

## Manage users and roles

Source: https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/users.md


When to use: a new analyst needs a correctly scoped account, an auditor asks who holds admin privileges, a compliance framework (SOC 2, HIPAA) requires a periodic access review, or you need to create or adjust a role, all from a scriptable terminal instead of the web UI.

### Prerequisites

- A Splunk account with the `edit_user` and `edit_roles` capabilities (the `admin` role has both).
- Role names from `splunkctl users roles list`.
- For `create` in scripts: the password on stdin from a secret manager, not on the command line.

### Synopsis

```text
splunkctl users list [--filter SUBSTRING] [--limit N] [--offset N]
splunkctl users get <NAME>
splunkctl users create --name <NAME> --roles <ROLE,ROLE> [--password TEXT | --password-stdin] [--email TEXT] [--realname TEXT] [--yes]
splunkctl users update <NAME> [--roles ROLE,ROLE] [--email TEXT] [--realname TEXT] [--default-app APP] [--password TEXT | --password-stdin] [--set KEY=VALUE]... [--yes]
splunkctl users delete <NAME> [--yes]

splunkctl users roles list [--filter SUBSTRING] [--limit N] [--offset N]
splunkctl users roles get <NAME>
splunkctl users roles create <NAME> [--capabilities LIST] [--imported-roles LIST] [--search-indexes LIST] [--search-filter TEXT] [--default-app APP] [--set KEY=VALUE]... [--yes]
splunkctl users roles update <NAME> [same flags as roles create] [--yes]
splunkctl users roles delete <NAME> [--yes]
```

### Workflow

#### List and inspect users and roles

```bash
splunkctl users list
splunkctl users list --filter svc
splunkctl users get admin
splunkctl users roles list
splunkctl users roles get power
```

Expected result: one row per user with `name`, `email`, and `roles`; one row per role with its capabilities (`roles get` shows the full, untruncated detail).

#### Create a user

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: a new account that can log in with the given roles. Preview with `splunkctl users create --name jdoe --roles user --email jdoe@example.com`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl users get jdoe`.

```bash
splunkctl users create --name jdoe --roles user --email jdoe@example.com --yes
openssl rand -base64 16 \
  | splunkctl users create --name jdoe --password-stdin --roles user --email jdoe@example.com --yes
vault kv get -field=pw secret/splunk \
  | splunkctl users create --name jdoe --roles user --password-stdin --yes
splunkctl users create --name jdoe --password 's3cret' --roles user --yes
splunkctl users get jdoe
```

Expected result: the user exists with the `user` role. The password comes from one of three places:

| Method | Command | When to use |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| Interactive prompt | omit `--password` | TTY sessions (default); hidden prompt with confirmation |
| Stdin pipe | `--password-stdin` | Scripts, CI/CD, secret managers |
| CLI flag | `--password` | Quick one-offs only; the value is visible in `ps` and `/proc` |

#### Update a user

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: the user's roles, email, display name, default app, or password change immediately. Preview with `splunkctl users update jdoe --roles 'user,power'`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl users get jdoe`.

```bash
splunkctl users update jdoe --roles 'user,power' --yes
splunkctl users update jdoe --email jdoe@corp.example --realname "Jane Doe" --default-app search --yes
openssl rand -base64 16 | splunkctl users update jdoe --password-stdin --yes
splunkctl users update jdoe --set tz=UTC --yes
```

Expected result: `--roles` replaces the whole role list. `update` prompts for a password only when you pass `--password` or `--password-stdin`. Role changes take effect on the user's next login; no restart is needed. `--set` passes any other user attribute as `KEY=VALUE`.

#### Delete a user

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: the account is removed and can no longer log in. Preview with `splunkctl users delete jdoe`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl users list --filter jdoe`.

```bash
splunkctl users get jdoe --json > jdoe-before.json
splunkctl users delete jdoe
splunkctl users delete jdoe --yes
```

#### Create or change a role

> **Safety:** Target is the Splunk host in the active profile. Impact: every user holding the role gains or loses capabilities and index access at next login; `roles delete` removes the role from the instance. Preview with `splunkctl users roles create soc_analyst --imported-roles user --search-indexes 'auth,firewall'`, apply by adding `--yes`, and verify with `splunkctl users roles get soc_analyst`.

```bash
splunkctl users roles create soc_analyst \
    --imported-roles user --search-indexes 'auth,firewall' \
    --capabilities 'schedule_search,edit_search_schedule_window' --default-app search --yes
splunkctl users roles update soc_analyst --search-filter 'NOT sourcetype=hr' --yes
splunkctl users roles update soc_analyst --set srchDiskQuota=500 --yes
splunkctl users roles delete soc_analyst --yes
```

Expected result: `roles get soc_analyst` shows the capabilities, imported roles, allowed indexes, search filter, and default app. Lists are comma-separated.

#### Audit privileged accounts

```bash
splunkctl users roles list --json \
  | jq '[.[] | select(.capabilities | index("admin_all_objects")) | .name]'
```

Expected result: the names of every role that carries `admin_all_objects`; cross-check holders with `splunkctl users list --json`.

#### Run a periodic access review

```bash
splunkctl users list --json | jq '.[] | {name, roles, email}' > review.json
splunkctl users roles list --json | jq '.[] | {name, capabilities}' >> review.json
```

Expected result: one file with every user, their roles, and every role's capabilities, ready to attach to the review ticket. `--json` output also suits compliance scripts and LLM agent tool chains.

### Troubleshooting

- `permission` on `create`, `update`, or `roles`: the account lacks `edit_user` or `edit_roles`.
- `not_found` on `get`, `update`, or `delete`: usernames are case-sensitive; find the exact name with `splunkctl users list --filter <part>`.
- `http` error on `create` mentioning the password: the server's password policy rejected it; generate a longer one.
- `http` error on `create` or `update` naming a role: the role does not exist; check `splunkctl users roles list`.
- `conflict` on `create` or `roles create`: the user or role already exists; use `update`.
- `--password-stdin` read an empty line: nothing was piped; the command reads exactly one line from stdin.
- Usage error (exit 2) on `create`: `--name` and `--roles` are required.

### See also

- [Audit changes and attest RBAC](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/audit.md)
- [Check server health and topology](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/server.md), for the authentication provider and role mapping
- [Log in through browser SAML](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/auth.md)
- [Administer SOAR users and roles](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/guides/soar-admin.md)
- [Command reference: users](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/commands/users.md)
